Introduction The topics are covered with particular attention to the new technical features required for passing the various tests introduced by new legislation. The descriptions and operating information provided are limited to a discussion of principles, rules and minimum precautions. For information on repair methods and vehicle specifications, see the specific sections on repair procedures. Aerodynamics The styling of the new car is designed to reflect great personality and originality and improves on the attributes of roominess, practicality and sturdiness achieved by previous models. The front, sides, rear and underbody were developed with particular attention to aerodynamics and allow outstanding drag coefficient values. The following values are an example: Version with basic specification: - drag coefficient CX = 0.32 - drag coefficient for area CX x S = 0.7574 These values are the result of road testing and measurements carried out in a wind tunnel. These results contribute to the noiselessness of the vehicle and significantly reduce wind noise. They also allow fuel saving. Safety The main aim of car manufacturers is definitely the total safety of the driver and passengers. To adapt the vehicle to highly demanding European and international market regulations, the new vehicle was designed with great attention to detail in order to achieve an optimum response in all situations. Passive safety A vehicle''s passive safety is the collection of technical and product solutions designed to protect the occupants of the vehicle in the case of an accident. The search for excellent performance has led to the introduction of design and construction solutions on the new vehicle that represent the state of the art in the field of passive safety. The occupant protection system The occupant protection system is composed of the following features fitted as standard on all trim levels: - the front protection system includes the electronic control unit, dual activation stage twin (driver and passenger) front air bags, driver and passenger knee bag, front seat belts with pretensioned buckle and load limiter in the reel, a control unit and safety sensor on the front tunnel, a additional decentralised impact detection sensor in the headlamp carrier crossmember, seat belt unfastened sensors for the front seats, occupant presence sensor on the passenger seat and passenger air bag manual disabling switch. - the chest/pelvic side protection system comprises two side bags in the front seats and two head/window bags along the roof side members - 3 point rear seat belts for all 3 rear seats. For more information on the Air Bag system See descriptions 5580C AIR BAG SYSTEM The solutions adopted in the design and manufacture of the seats, the dashboard and the interior panels and fittings increase the degree of passive safety of the vehicle. For more information on these topics, refer to the specific chapters. Resistance to impacts All the features relating to Passive Safety have been developed in order to offer the maximum protection for the occupant in all possible impact situations at high speed: - frontal impact - rear impact - side impact - roll over The behaviour of the bodyshell in crash tests has more than adequately satisfied the international safety standards. Pedestrian protection The style of the front part of the vehicle has been developed taking into account the protection of pedestrians as required by the most recent international legislation. The shapes are smooth and rounded and there are no unsafe projections for the safety of pedestrians. The ample surface area of the bonnet minimizes the risk of contact between pedestrian''s heads and the rigid front pillars. The most rigid components are located inside the engine compartment a suitable distance away from the bonnet in order to allow the bonnet skin to absorb the energy forces of the impact with the pedestrian''s head. Protection against fire At the end of the 90''s with the introduction of new European regulations regarding crash tests and with the introduction of fuel injection systems, the need to seriously redefine the design of the bodyshell and the layout of the various systems on the vehicle. The entire vehicle, from the bodyshell to the various components is therefore subject to the rigorous observance of the most recent and most stringent internal regulations regarding protection against fire. Fuel system and evaporation control system and fps Special care has been taken over the layout to locate potentially critical devices outside of the impact area, also the routing of the various systems, which has been carefully considered from the earliest stages, is very well protected in order to reduce potentially critical situations. - The underbody fuel and evaporation control pipes are arranged parallel to the extremely strong underfloor side member. There is also a specific plastic duct to protect against accidental contact (stone chipping, etc.). In the engine compartment on the right hand side, metal sections of pipe have been used to prevent any fuel leaks in the case of contact during an impact. - The petrol versions have a returnless fuel system which allows the fuel return pipe to the tank to be dispensed with reducing the risk of leaks. - The evaporation control system active charcoal filter is located in the left rear wheel arch, in other words in an area that is not vulnerable and is near the tank. - There is an inertia switch on the petrol and diesel versions (FPS - Fire Prevention System) that immediately switches off the engine a few milliseconds after the start of the impact. - The plastic tank exceeds not only national but also foreign legal requirements. It is located in an area protected in the case of a collision and has the capacity to withstand any deformation without the risk of fuel leaks. Also, being plastic, there is no risk of explosion if the vehicle is on fire. Engine compartment electrical equipment - The positive battery terminal is not facing the direction of travel and the risk of short circuiting in the case of a frontal impact is thereby greatly reduced. - The main section of the high power positive leads is directly on the positive battery pole in a maxi fuse box. This solution prevents the presence of sections of cable not protected by fuses and therefore exposed to accidental short circuiting. There is also a series of automatic sectioning devices operated by the inertia switch (FPS) which, in the initial milliseconds following a serious impact, detach the battery connection to the high power leads averting the risk of a short circuit. - All the main cables are electrically insulated and fitted inside corrugated covers for mechanical protection against the possible risk of abrasion. - The electrical insulation of the starter motor/battery power lead is made from a material with good resistance to abrasion and cutting with the routing using special fastenings and protected by metal brackets. Passenger compartment interior electrical equipment - All the cables are protected by fuses located in the body computer control unit on the left side of the dashboard. - The routing of all the cables has been designed to prevent pinching during fitting or interference during operation and to reduce the potential risk of short circuiting to a minimum. Exhaust pipe - All the components that could suffer from radiated heat (reduced by the presence of a special shield) from the exhaust system have been located a suitable distance away. - Large metal shields on the underbody make it possible to protect the surrounding parts from the heat produced by the exhaust pipe (tank, handbrake cables, flexible supports). The structure of the vehicle The chassis The chassis represents a radial structural change compared with the previous chassis of the 156. The chassis contains several ets of longitudinal box section structural elements, connected to one another by transverse elements and finished off by dashboard and floor panels. The floor panel box sections are integrated with the bodyshell elements, finishing off a perfectly integrated and solid structure. The absorption of energy from a frontal or rear impact is mainly carried out along the two load lines consisting of the front struts, engine mounting frame, rear struts, underfloor side members and side members. The continuity, for the entire length of the vehicle, of these three parts guarantees gradual defornation in accordance with the severity of the impact. In addition, the connection between the struts and the engine suspension frame contributes in distributing the load towards the deformed obstacle in the optimum way. The high resistance material and differentiated thicknesses of the front and rear side members are designed to support the forces developed by the front and rear crossmembers in the case of impacts at low speed without damage and, at the same time, to allow the absorption of all the impact energy in impacts at high speed without the passenger compartment being deformed. There is a box section crossmember at the front with controlled deformation collapsible struts (crash box), whilst there is a very thick crossmember at the rear with a collapsible open section. Both crossmembers are made from high resistance steel and are bolted onto the floor panel in order to facilitate servicing operations. Above the engine and in front of the H nodes there are a further two struts that intercept the stresses arriving from the top part of the vehicle through their deformation, especially when the vehicle crashes into the back of a lorry. There is a special box structure at the rear, immediately behind the rear seat backrest, constituting an extremely important structural element for the torsional strength of the bodyshell. The galvanizing treatment on both sides of all the chassis and bodywork structural elements and the use in some areas of increased galvanizing thickness panels, prevents the risk of rust, both structural and aesthetic and therefore guarantees the maintenance of structural performance for the entire life of the vehicle. The bodywork The bodyshell basically features three very important technical-technological factors: the use of high performance materials, the use of multi-thickness panels and the use of laser welding. The outer bodyshell, also to a great extent made from high resistance material (58% of the weight of the entire bodyshell is made from high resistance steel, whilst a further 7% of the weight of the entire bodyshell involves the use of dual-phase steel), represents a structure featuring numerous longitudinal, lateral and transverse box sections strengthened by internal reinforcement and featuring highly resistant sections. Dual-phase steel belongs to a family of high resistance steel which, on account of its metallurgical properties and chemical composition, features very good mechanical resistance properties (ferrite phase - very high yield and breaking loads) and excellent moulding properties (martensite phase - drawing depth) and are therefore particularly suitable for use on complex geometry panels which the bodyshell elements often are. Like for the chassis previously, the bodyshell has also made use of tailored-blank technology, in other words sheets of multi-thickness laser welded panels for the constructions of the most important structural elements, such as the side frame and the roof rib. Multi-thickness panels, compared with more traditional configurations where the elements are one single thickness with added local reinforcements, allows important improvements in terms of weight and technological sheel-metal working process (reduction in the number of weld spots). Laser seam welding, used both for indefinite panels (in the tailored-blanks mentioned above) and for finished elements (join between the roof outer cover and the side panels), which are then connected to one another without a continuity solution (in place of traditional spot welding) makes it possible to produce high quality, good performance structural joins. All these elements give the structure an extremely good torsional-bending strength and contribute to supporting the forces created by the centre side members in longitudinal impacts, whilst they play an important role in side impacts. An important contribution made by the good torsional strength is the elimination of creaking due to the torsion of the bodyshell and the interior and exterior fittings in operating conditions. The doors The front and rear side doors are secured to the bodyshell by hinges and locks well above the minimum legislative standards and make an important contribution in both frontal and side impacts. A double high resistance steel lengthwise reinforcement along the waistline stabilizes the entire structure of the door and contributes to the non-deformability of the passenger compartment in a frontal impact. Experiments have confirmed that the doors do not open accidentally in various types of impacts, at the same time guaranteeing easy opening after an impact. Behaviour in terms of side impacts has improved with suitably sized ultra high resistant dual-phase steel crossmembers on all 4 doors. The bonnet Various safety measures have been introduced. There are preset collapse lines which, together with specific retaining hooks on the hinges, prevent it penetrating the windscreen in the case of an impact. Windscreen and rearscreen The fixed windows are a further safety feature. To increase the vehicle safety level, the windscreen is in laminated glass. This solution prevents the glass from shattering if struck by stones or gravel to assure visibility at all times and above all to offer a high level of protection if struck with the head. The windscreen and the rearscreen are bonded to the bodyshell, thereby contributing to increasing the structural strength of the vehicle: the seals flush with the bodywork contribute to reducing the noise due to oncoming air (wind noise). The bumpers They have been designed to provide excellent protection in the case of minor impacts. The rear crossmembers right behind the outer shell of both bumpers and the absorbers (for the rear with collapsible cell inserts) positioned between the bumper shell and the crossmember, limit damage in impacts at up to 4 km/h. The underdashboard crossmember The crossmember made from mangnesium to make it light and integrate with the other sub-systems, is located between the two front pillars underneath the dashboard with the shape reproducing the entire upper dashboard. It guarantees a sturdy connection not only between the pillars but also with the floor to which it is connected by means of two struts. This configuration contributes significantly to ensuring the non-deformability of the entire front area of the passenger compartment during head-on and side impacts. Because it also acts as a support structure for the steering column, it prevents the steering wheel moving back and upwards during all types of frontal impact. The crossmember under the dashboard also has the function of contributing to the release of the pedals; in effect, an appropriate size bracket is securely fastened to the crossmember by the releasable pedal assembly triggers that is positioned in such a way as to release the brake and clutch pedals if they are retracted; this cancels out the thrust of the pedals on the occupants tibia and protects the survival space. New technology Laser For the first time on a Group vehicle the roof has been secured to the bodyshell by laser sources for a total of 2.8 m of the vehicle. This means perfect matching along the entire length of the roof and, above all, the possibility of using increased resistance sections (lasers work on one side of the panel only) allowing improved performance. Panel assembly join Laser technology (Comau-Agliaser patent) is also used in the preparation of the doors which benefit from the same advantages with more extended and more homogenous panels. Medium frequency welding Medium frequency welding has been used extensively for the assembly of the bodyshell allowing the use of more preformed materials and very thick panels. In this case too this is the first application on a Group model. Automation The body panel assembly line is highly automated with 127 robots which allow 81% of the welding to be carried out completely automatically thereby guaranteeing constantly high quality. Geometry Along the bodyshell assembly line, in order to guarantee constant quality over a period of time, there are 2 opto-electronic measuring stations that allow 100% measurement of production at 84 "critical" points (with constant checks guaranteed) and a new measuring station checking 490 "key" points sampled daily. Possibility of damage and repair of impacts at low speed Special attention has been paid to impacts at low speed to limit damage to the front section of the vehicle, thereby preventing costly repairs to the chassis and cooling module. The chassis structural elements (struts) have been designed in such a way that they are not deformed in this type of impact in spite of the forces exchanged with the parts in front subjected to the impact against the obstacle. There is a strong crossmember behind the front bumper made from a high resistance material that is capable of absorbing all the typical impact energy in a low speed accident thereby preventing damage to the most expensive components inside the engine compartment. The crossmember is bolted to the front side members to facilitate the operations of removing and refitting. During the first stages of the impact the front crossmember starts to deform absorbing a considerable amount of energy and moving backwards parallel to itself without collapse instability that could damage the radiant pack behind; as the situation progresses, the deformation is transmitted to the absorption elements (crash box), in other words the longitudinal box sections that produce controlled high absorption efficiency controlled folding. The cooling module has been located a safe distance from the actual crossmember and from the engine layout so that in the case of low speed impacts there is space for it to move backwards without being involved in the damage. The new feature is that the cooling module is supported by the headlamp carrier crossmember from above and the engine frame crossmember from below by means of releasable fastenings that allow it to move backwards without deforming the attachment feet in the case of an impact, in effect the pressure transmitted by the duct to the strong side parts of the reservoirs in the initial moments is sufficient to release the fastenings. The release can be restored without special operations and does NOT require repair activities. In this way the labour time and therefore cost is considerably lower than conventional solutions. The vehicle is also fitted with a collapsible system for the fastenings securing the front headlamps to the headlamp carrier crossmember. Following an impact the fastenings yield and the entire headlamp casing retracts without any damage to it. To restore the vehicle simply tighten the new fastening tabs to the headlamp casing. The rear part of the vehicle is similar to the front: in this case too there is an extremely strong crossmember made from a ultra resistant material which contains highly efficient impact absorbers near the rear side members. In thise case the absorption elements are the only components to replace in the case of low speed shunts. Sound insulation General specifications To meet EEC standards, the vehicle''s exterior noise levels must be lower than 74 decibels. Driving comfort and living conditions inside the passenger compartment have been improved by: - optimising the body through a thorough examination of all parts subject to noise, which have been made stiffer and fastened more securely; - choosing contact materials with great care; - by improving the insulation against noise transmitted from the road surface, from mechanical parts and from the suspension; - by taking great care over parts assembly, aerodynamics and all parts with shapes that affect acoustic comfort, such as door handles, door mirrors, bumpers and other outlines; - by fitting new generation engines with high-tech features designed to improve acoustic/vibrational factors; - by fitting a new barycentric engine mounting. Another area of improvement has been the passenger compartment insulation. The following action has been taken: - highly efficient sound-absorbent materials with optmum thickness and layout on the vehicle; - fitting of a sound-absorbent undershield in the lower part of the engine compartment for acoustic insulation; - elimination of acoustic holes (areas where sound can pass between the engine compartment and passenger compartment) by fitting double-lipped seals, thicker rubber plugs; - by fitting the various sound-insulation parts together more tightly to avoid uncovered areas; - extensive use of sound-absorbent seals; - sound-proofed coating of panels with heat-bonded materials applied before painting; - lining of the bulkhead and front steps to remove the sensation of the engine''s presence; - application of heat-expanding materials inside the box sections prior to painting to reduce noise transmission. During body cataphoresis process, the volume of these materials expands ten times to fill the box section effectively. - lining the boot compartment appropriately to reduce rolling noise; - carefully examining the fitting and size of parts liable to squeak such as the facia, heater and seats: the anchorage and fastening points have been reinforced. To maintain the high level of acoustic comfort achieved, the specifications adopted during manufacture must be restored exactly in the event of repair. PROTECTION OF THE BODYSHELL Introduction The vehicle body is designed to withstand for many years any environmental attack to the interior, not visible but potential subject to corrosion, and exterior, particularly subject to damage that may affect the exerior appearance of the vehicle. In order to achieve these objectives specific activities have been carried out during all the development stages of the model including both the design and the production process using the most up to date and innovative methods (FMEA, Robust Design). These instruments have been used to apply the guidelines for special anti-corrosion standards that ensure completely accessibility of the bodyshell to the protection and painting processes (in particular the rust prevention cataphoretic painting process) and the correct shape of each element designed to prevent any possible build up of dampness in the box sections and allow the perfect sealing of all the panel joins. Galvanising The bodyshell basic protection level has been defined in parallel to the design and process criteria: 85% of the bodyshell is made up of panels galvanized on both sides. In particular, all the structural elements of the chassis are 100% galvanized. Out of these, the structures defined as safety structures (suspension mountings, seat belt reinforcements, ect.) are made from high thickness zinc galvanized panels (20 microns compared with 8 for standard galvanized panels). The bodywork is made totally from panels galvanized on both sides for the moving parts (covers and frames) and for all the elements of the fixed outer panels, including those that make up the door stops, visible with the doors open. All the anti-corrosion provision has been subjected to laboratory tests and checked on the vehicle with FOR-LIFE tests which were carried out in special test areas that reproduce the most stringent conditions of the northern European market. The total galvanizing of the outer bodyshell makes it possible, together with the protection package provided by the painting process, to produce the 3 year goal without cosmetic corrosion points. The protection package provided by galvanized panels and cataphoresis for all the structures makes it possible to exceed the 8 year vehicle life without panel perforation in the most harsh climates of northern Europe and to comply with the European legislation regarding safety points (10 years with structural weaknesses). Painting A new painting system has been launched for the production of the vehicle designed and produced using the most recent technological innovations available on the market both as far as the adoption of application systems is concerned and in terms of the choice of products. This innovation involves the introduction, for the entire colour range, of water-based enamels and the use of PUR 2K transparent resin in place of traditional products. This last solution, in addition to resulting in a reduction in the emission of organic compounds into the atmosphere, improves the final aesthetic appearance, allowing the original shiny finish to last better and endowing it with improved resistance to chemical and mechanical attack such as, for example, better resistance to the tiny scratches caused by the action of the brushes in automatic car washes. A - paint product supplier B - enamel colour and type C - code D - type of product to be used for touching up and painting in the event of service operations Re-apply the wax oil treatment if box section parts are replaced during service. Recycling of materials Main specifications According to EEC ELV (End of Life Vehicles) directives, all metallic and non-metallic parts must be recovered from the vehicle and reused, 80% to produce new material and 5% for recovered energy. Nowadays, some 75% of a vehicle''s weight is made up of metal that can easily be recovered by melting when different metals can be separated by heating to their different melting points. All the remaining part of the vehicle, amounting to 25% by weight, must be recovered before this stage. The solution to the problem of recycling plastics is resolved at the design stage: the possibility of re-using the material on future components must be assessed at this time: The aims to be considered at the design stage include: - ease of component disassembly; - choice of noble materials in the recyclable polymer chain (giving priority to parts made up of a single family, e.g. PP). Recycling does not allow the production of a part that is the same as the original part because the material may not be able to guarantee the necessary levels of reliability or it may not be financially viable. Plastics may be recycled in a cascade pattern. For example: - insulating material for the building industry is obtained from seat padding; - the material used to line the wheel arches is obtained from the bumpers and then goes on to produce sound-proofing elements. In the end, it becomes a fuel for energy production. This model has been designed to ensure that all its plastic and elastomer parts (rubbers) weighing over 50 grams are marked with coded symbols to identify the material during recycling and also to ensure that all its components are recyclable. In particular, the impacts that could be exerted on the environment both during the life cycle of the product and during the scrapping stage are already analyzed during the design stage. In some cases the choice of materials has been made using an innovative evaluation system known as L.C.A. (Life Cycle Assessment) which makes it possible to assess the effects on the environment globally, taking into account not only the engineering and industrial specifications of the materials, but also the environmental critical areas during the production of the raw materials during usage and at the end of life. Great emphasis has been placed for this model on improving its recyclability: technological solutions in single materials have been favoured and the polymer families present have been further reduced. The recycling therefore involves three successive generations of vehicles contributing to savings in raw materials. Other materal reuse processes are also being examined outside the motor industry, following the lead taken by the F.A.Re (Fiat Auto Recycling) partnership in the Eighties and Nineties. Another important point to note concerns the use of heavy metals in the motor industry. The metals in question are hexavalent chrome (Cr6), Mercury (Hg), Cadmium (Cd) and lead (Pb). These are banned (Cr6) or permitted only in tiny amounts when their use must be indicated by labelling or by including information in the documents supplied with the vehicle. The tables in the chapter "GENERAL INFORMATION AND TECHNICAL DATA - OPERATING DATA" show symbols for and descriptions of recyclable materials present on the vehicle. This is to ensure that the best available products are used to wash the interior, paint plastic parts and carry out repairs, bonding etc. The aim is to avoid the possibility of damage by using incompatible products. Labelling also allows organic materials to be selected on the basis of their chemical composition. During service, it is also advisable to separate materials on the basis of their composition to ensure that they can be recycled more easily. The system can recognize the transponder and switch off the alarm system in this way. The siren is connected to the Body Computer Node via the A-Bus dialogue line. The siren is operated and controlled by the Body Computer Node by means of a series of coded messages; in the case of a failure the Body Computer node detects and memorizes the causes of the malfunction. The siren is equipped with a battery whose charge is guaranteed in the presence of a +15 supply from the ignition with the alarm system switched off and is managed by the actual siren; the activation/end of charge command is given by the Body Computer Results of the tests 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT All OK Problems encountered Operation Connect the diagnostic equipment ot the diagnostic socket and check for the presence of the siren at the Body Computer Node in the parameters ambient Move on to Step 2 Siren not present Check the conformity of the vehicle 2 SIREN ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the power supply for the siren is correct and check the continuity and insulation for the A-BUS serial line between the Body Computer Node and the siren by carrying out the See Test 5580EB SIREN FUNCTIONAL TEST Move on to Step 3 3 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT All OK Problems encountered Operation Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket and check the following at the Body Computer Node in parameters ambient . the correct activation of the siren . the condition of the A-Bus serial line Move on to Step 4 The siren is not activated Replace the siren See Test 5580E40 ANTI-THEFT DEVICE SIREN - R+R Serial line broken Renew serial line See E7015 ALARM 4 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis The fault persists Replace Body Computer Op. 5505A32 BODY COMPUTER - R.R

When the alarm is switched on using the remote control, the system is activated correctly but the volumetric sensors do not intervene. 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Carry out a driving cycle simulating a hilly / urban route with frequent gear changes and 4-5 departures from a standstill to heat up the clutch/engine assemblies. Assess the manoeuvrability of the gearbox by carrying out the following with the vehicle stationary and the engine idling: - engagements of reverse gear with manoeuvre times increasing from 1 to 4 seconds; - engagements of forward speeds; carry out the manoeuvres by fully depressing the clutch pedal to the end of travel position. - Eliminate any obstacles to the correct clutch pedal travel (positioning of mats, interference of cables, etc.) Move on to Step 1 The problem only occurs when certain speeds are engaged. Proceed as instructed in the See table C002 GEAR ENGAGEMENT OR RELEASE DIFFICULT 1 CLUTCH LEVER TRAVEL CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check, inside the engine compartment, that when the clutch pedal is pressed the clutch control lever on the gearbox completes the correct travel. Move on to Step 9 Clutch lever on gearbox travel incomplete. Move on to Step 2. 2 VISUAL INSPECTION FOR LEAKS OR SEEPAGE ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION - Visually inspect the operating cylinder and pipes. - Check that there is no seepage, leaks or damage. Move on to Step 3 Leaks, damage or seepage from pipes and/or hydraulic connectors. Repair the defective or damaged components. 3 CHECK FOR AIR IN THE HYDRAULIC CLUTCH CIRCUIT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Using the operating cylinder bleed screw, check that there is no air in the circuit. Move on to Step 4 Air in the circuit. Bleed the air Op. 0010T67 HYDRAULIC CLUTCH SYSTEM - BLEED AIR 4 CLUTCH CONTROL CYLINDER CHECK (ON VEHICLE) ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION - Release the cylinder from the clutch control lever, keeping it connected to the hydraulic system. - Press the pedal producing the thrust pressure and check the push rod travel. - Using a drift, retract the push rod checking that it travels freely. Move on to Step 5 Clutch control cylinder malfunction. Remove the clutch control cylinder Op. 1820B30 CLUTCH HYDRAULIC ACTUATOR - R.R. and move on to Step 6. 5 ENGINE AND GEARBOX CASING ALIGNMENT CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check for the centering pins on the engine block checking whether the flexible couplings have become loose if the centering pins are not present. Move on to Step 6 The centering pins are missing. Correct the problem by inserting the centering pins The flexible couplings have become loose. Ensure the flexible couplings are correctly closed. 6 CLUTCH CONTROL CYLINDER CHECK (WITH GEARBOX REMOVED) ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION With the part at the bench, apply pressure (using compressed air) and check the push rod travel (the test mirrors what was done in the vehicle). N.B.: This test is designed to ensure that the problem is due to the cylinder and not to the pipes or the pump. Move on to Step 7 Clutch control cylinder malfunction. Replace the clutch control cylinder Op. 1820B30 CLUTCH HYDRAULIC ACTUATOR - R.R. 7 CLUTCH PEDAL TRAVEL CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION With the system disconnected, check that the travel is correct when the pedal is pressed and released. Move on to Step 8 Hydraulic pump malfunction Replace the pump Op. 1820B20 MASTER CYLINDER (PUMP) - R + R Flexible pipe from clutch reservoir to pump worn or distorted. Replace the pipe Op. 1820B40 HOSE FROM CLUTCH RESERVOIR TO MASTER CYLINDER (PUMP) - R + R Flexible supply pipe to clutch control cylinder worn or distorted. Replace the pipe Op. 1820B56 RIGID PIPE FROM VIBRATION DAMPER TO SLAVE CYLINDER - R R 8 CLUTCH PEDAL CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Clutch pedal disconnected from transmission Op. 3330B26 CLUTCH PEDAL - R+R check that the travel is free and there is no sticking or hardening. Move on to Step 9 Clutch pedal clearance or hardening. Replace the pedal Op. 3330B26 CLUTCH PEDAL - R+R 9 PLATE LEVER AND BEARING CHECK (WITH GEARBOX REMOVED) ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION After the gearbox has been removed, check that there is no hardening of the lever (as a result of dirt or insufficient greasing) and that the plate bearing slides freely in its housing and shows no signs of damage. move on to Step 10 The presence of dirt or wear due to insufficient greasing does not allow the plate bearing to slide correctly. Replace the faulty or damaged components. 10 CLUTCH ASSEMBLY CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Visually inspect the state of the clutch assembly, making sure there are no breaks and/or signs of overheating on the plate, obvious deterioration of the driven disc or grease/oil on the friction surfaces. move on to Step 11 Obvious deterioration of the clutch disc and/or plate broken. Replace the assembly Op. 1810A24 CLUTCH - R + R WITH GEARBOX REMOVED Oil or grease on the disc. Remove the oil or grease from the disc. Flexible coupling springs weak or broken. Replace the mechanism Op. 1810A24 CLUTCH - R + R WITH GEARBOX REMOVED Break at the base of the clutch disc friction material support segments. Replace the clutch plate Op. 1810A24 CLUTCH - R + R WITH GEARBOX REMOVED 10 CLUTCH ASSEMBLY CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Visually inspect the state of the clutch assembly, making sure there are no breaks and/or signs of overheating on the plate, obvious deterioration of the driven disc or grease/oil on the friction surfaces. move on to Step 11 Obvious deterioration of the clutch disc and/or plate broken. Replace the assembly Op. 1810A24 CLUTCH - R + R WITH GEARBOX REMOVED Oil or grease on the disc. Remove the oil or grease from the disc. Flexible coupling springs weak or broken. Replace the assembly Op. 1810A24 CLUTCH - R + R WITH GEARBOX REMOVED Break at the base of the clutch disc friction material support segments. Replace the assembly Op. 1810A24 CLUTCH - R + R WITH GEARBOX REMOVED 11 CLUTCH SLIDING SPLINED HUB CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the following, in order: - for excess grease on the clutch plate hub bushes and the gearbox main shaft. - the condition of the main shaft hub. move on to Step 12 Main shaft damaged. Replace the main shaft. Hub worn. Replace the hub. Excess grease on the bushes. Remove the excess grease from the bushes. Gearbox shaft centering bush worn / half locked. Replace the bush 12 CLUTCH SLIDING SPLINED HUB CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the flywheel. In particular, check: the state of the surface; wear; cuts; presence of grease/oil on the disc surfaces; signs of overheating. End of diagnosis Flywheel damaged. Replace the flywheel Op. 1024B10 ENGINE FLYWHEEL - R + R FOR VERSIONS WITH MANUAL GEARBOX Presence of dust in the flywheel friction seal. Remove the dust from the flywheel friction seal.

With the vehicle moving, if the handbrake is accidentally operated this is not indicated by the acoustic warning. The instrument panel node acquires the handbrake switch status and vehicle speed signal from the network. If the handbrake is activated and the vehicle speed is above 4 km/h, an acoustic warning is issued. This function can be enabled/disabled using the MODE +/- buttons in the control panel. Make sure that the function has not been disabled by mistake by the user 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner Plus or Smart diagnostic equipment and check, in the active diagnosis ambient, that the buzzer is working properly Move on to Step 1 The buzzer is not working. Replace the instrument panel node Op. 5560B10 CONTROL PANEL - R+R 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Keeping the Examiner diagnostic equipment connected check, in the parameters ambient, that the handbrake switch status learning is correct Move on to Step 3 Malfunction in the acquisition of the handbrake switch status. Move on to Step 2 2 ELECTRICAL CONNECTION CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the electrical connections between the handbrake switch and the Body Computer See E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL Also check that the handbrake switch is not faulty. Move on to Step 3 1. Connections faulty 1. Restore the correct connections See E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL 2. Handbrake switch faulty. 2. Replace the handbrake switch Op. 5550D18 HANDBRAKE ON WARNING LIGHT SWITCH - R+R 3 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment and check the following at the body computer node: that there are no errors at the C-CAN line; that there are no speedometer signal errors. Move on to Step 4 1. Error detected at the C-CAN line. 1. Continue following the instructions for the diagnostic equipment 2. Error detected at the speedometer signal. 2. Proceed as instructed in the See table K003 SPEEDOMETER NOT WORKING 4 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Keeping the Examiner diagnostic equipment connected, check the following at the instrument panel node: that there are no errors at the B-CAN line; that there are no speedometer signal errors. Move on to Step 5 1. Error detected at the B-CAN line. 1. Continue following the instructions for the diagnostic equipment 2. Error detected at the speedometer signal. 2. Proceed as instructed in the See table K003 SPEEDOMETER NOT WORKING 5 ELECTRICAL CONNECTION CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the electrical connections between the instrument panel and the Body Computer See E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL Move on to Step 6 Connections faulty. Restore the correct connections See E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL 6 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present. End of diagnosis. The fault persists. Replace Body Computer Op. 5505A32 BODY COMPUTER - R.R

- of the bush securing the camber rod to the steering knuckle Move on to Step 4 Bush securing the camber rod to the crossmember not intact Replacement of camber rod in accordance with the Op. 4410B68 LOWER SWINGING ARM(ONE), LH OR RH OF FRONT SUSPENSION - R R -CHECK WHEEL ALIGNMENT SEPARATELY checking the camber values are correct Bush securing the camber rod to the steering knuckle not intact Replacement of rear stub axle, checking that the toe in values are correct 4 SHOCK ABSORBER EFFICIENCY CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the efficiency of the shock absorbers by carrying out manual compression manoeuvres (resting on the wheel arch by the centre of the wheel), which should be carried out on both sides of the vehicle. Move on to Step 5 Sudden return without damping Replace the shock absorber that is not working properly Op. 4420A12 REAR SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMENTLING/REBUILDING OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH R R 5 VEHICLE GEOMETRY CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation After replacing the shock absorbers, check the geometry End of diagnosis Geometry values do not conform Restore the geometry to the correct values Op. 4450A40 REAR WHEEL GEOMETRY - CHECK USING OPTICAL EQUIPMENT, INCLUDES ADJUSTMENT IF NECESSARY

When the steering is operated normally there is a hardening of the steering action to both the left and the right 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Carry out a test steering fully in various conditions to check the actual onset of the hardening in both directions. Visually inspect the power assisted steering fluid level in the reservoir. Move on to Step 1 1. Hardening in one direction only 1. Proceed as instructed in the See table H011 STEERING HARD / (IN ONE DIRECTION ONLY) 2. Power assisted steering fluid level too low. 2. Top up to the correct level, if there are leaks, continue as instructed in the See table X030 POWER ASSISTED STEERING SYSTEM FLUID LEAKS 1 CHECK ON TYPE OF PROBLEM ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Carry out a test steering fully in various conditions: check the way in which the problem starts. Continuous and constant hardening: move on to Step 2 1. Hardening only during idling. 1. Check for constrictions in the system flexible and rigid pipes. If necessary, replace the damaged parts, replacing all the seals, see Assembly Op. 4130B POWER STEERING HYDRAULIC SYTEM 2. Hardening in end of travel position. 2. Restore the correct vehicle geometry, see Assembly Op. 4450A WHEEL GEOMETRY 2 STEERING RODS AND ARMS CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the steering rods and arms. Move on to Step 3 1. Rods damaged or worn. 1. Replace the rods Op. 4110B10 STEERING LINKS - R+R ON VEHICLE - CHECK TOE-IN/TOE-OUT SEPARATELY 2. Arms damaged or worn. 2. Replace the steering box Op. 4120A10 STEERING BOX - R+R - CHECK WHEEL TOE-IN IF NECESSARY SEPARATELY 3 CHECK STEERING COLUMN BEARINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the steering column support bearings and that they are working properly. Move on to Step 4 Bearings worn or damaged Restore the efficiency of the steering column. If necessary, replace the bearings involved Op. 4110A30 SUPPORT WITH STEERING CONTROL SHAFTS - R+R 4 RACK AND PINION CLEARANCE CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the rack and pinion clearance with the steering column detached and the wheels straight. Move on to Step 5 Rack and pinion clearance too large Replace the steering box Op. 4120A10 5 RACK CLEARANCE AND STEERING BOX FASTENINGS CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the bushes-rack radial clearance. Check that the steering box fastening is correct. Move on to Step 6 1. Rack-bushes clearance too large. 1. Replace the steering box Op. 4120A10 2. Steering box fastening not correct. 2. Restore correct fastenings. 6 CHECK ON CORRECT TENSION OF DRIVE BELT AND CORRECT OPERATION OF POWER ASSISTED STEERING PUMP ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the tension of the power assisted steering pump drive belt is correct and that it is not worn. Also check that the power assisted steering pump is working properly. Move on to Step 7 1. Belt not correctly tensioned. 1. Restore correct belt tension Op. 1092C12 POWER STEERING PUMP DRIVE BELT - ADJUST TENSION 2. Belt worn. 2. Replace the belt Op. 1092C11 POWER STEERING PUMP DRIVE BELT - R.R. FOR VERSIONS WITH AIR CONDITIONER 3. Power assisted steering pump malfunction. 3. Replace the power assisted steering pump Op. 4130B24 POWER STEERING PUMP R R FOR VERSIONS WITH AIR CONDITIONER 7 STEERING WHEEL RETURN CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Refit all the components removed. Test the vehicle and check that the steering wheel returns correctly. End of diagnosis Poor steering wheel return. Restore the correct front wheel geometry Op. 4450A10 FRONT WHEEL GEOMETRY - CHECK USING OPTICAL EQUIPMENT - INCLUDES ADJUSTMENT IF NECESSARY

There are rapid oscillations in the steering on a straight road at speed 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION First of all, check that the tyres are the correct type, in good condition and correctly inflated. Also check that the wheel bolts are correctly tightened. Move on to Step 1 1. Tyre inflation pressure not correct. 1. Restore the correct tyre inflation pressure 2. Tyres unsuitable or worn 2. Replace the tyres 3. Wheel bolts not correctly tightened. 3. Tighten the wheel studs correctly. 1 WHEEL CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check: That the wheels are correctly balanced. The condition of the wheel rims (they should have dents or be distorted). Move on to Step 2 1. Wheels not balanced. 1. Balance the wheels correctly. 2. Wheel rims dented or distorted. 2. Replace the wheel rims. 2 ENGINE FLEXIBLE MOUNTINGS CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition and the centering of the engine frame, the engine flexible mountings and the engine side and gearbox side connecting rods. Move on to Step 3 1. Engine flexible mountings faulty. 1. Adjust the fastenings: loosen the bolts, centre them in their housings and tighten them to the recommended torque, see Assembly Op. 1008A POWER UNIT FASTENINGS 2. Engine side and gearbox side connecting rods faulty. 2. Adjust the fastenings: loosen the bolts, centre them in their housings and tighten them to the recommended torque, see Assembly Op. 1008C POWER UNIT REACTION ELEMENTS 3. Engine frame faulty. 3. Adjust the fastenings: loosen the bolts, centre them in their housings and tighten them to the recommended torque. Op. 4410D13 FRONT SUSPENSION CROSSMEMBER - R.R 3 CHECK ON CONDITION OF FLEXIBLE MOUNTINGS AND BUSHES ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the bushes and flexible mountings. In order: ball joints for steering box rods; bushes for upper and lower track control arms; flexible mountings for anti-roll bar. Move on to Step 4 1. Steering box rod ball joints worn or damaged. 1. Replace the rods Op. 4110B10 STEERING LINKS - R+R ON VEHICLE - CHECK TOE-IN/TOE-OUT SEPARATELY 2. Bushes for upper or lower arms worn or damaged 2. Replace the upper track control arms Op. 4410B72 FRONT SUSPENSION UPPER WISHBONES (LH AND RH) - R R - CHECK WHEEL ALIGNMENT SEPARATELY or the lower track control arms Op. 4410B43 LOWER TRACK CONTROL ARMS (WITH BALLJOINTS) FOR FRONT SUSPENSION (LEFT AND RIGHT) - R.R. - CHECK WHEEL ALIGNMENT SEPARATELY 3. Anti-roll bar mountings. 3. Replace the flexible mountings for anti-roll bar Op. 4410C16 FRONT SUSPENSION STABILIZER BAR JOINT BUSHES - REPLACE 4 SPRING SHOCK ABSORBER ASSEMBLY CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check: the condition of the shock absorbers and the springs and that they are working efficiently; the fastenings of the spring/shock absorber assembly. Move on to Step 5 1. Tightening not correct. 1. Renew the correct fastening. 2. Shock absorbers not working properly. 2. Replace the shock absorber involved Op. 4410A12 FRONT SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMANTLING/REASSEMBLY OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R 3. Springs not working properly. 3. Replace the spring involved Op. 4410A12 FRONT SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMANTLING/REASSEMBLY OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R 5 STEERING RODS AND ARMS CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the steering rods and arms. Move on to Step 6 1. Rods damaged or worn. 1. Replace the rods Op. 4110B10 STEERING LINKS - R+R ON VEHICLE - CHECK TOE-IN/TOE-OUT SEPARATELY 2. Arms damaged or worn. 2. Replace the steering box Op. 4130A10 POWER STEERING BOX - R+R 6 INTERMEDIATE SHAFT DAMPER CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the intermediate shaft torsion damper is working properly. Move on to Step 7 Torsion damper not working properly. Replace the intermediate shaft Op. 4110A46 INTERMEDIATE SHAFT FOR CONNECTION TO STEERING BOX - R.R 7 CHECK STEERING COLUMN BEARINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the steering column supports and that they are working properly. End of diagnosis Bearings worn or damaged Restore the efficiency of the steering column. If necessary, replace the bearings involved Op. 4110A31 SUPPORT WITH STEERING CONTROL SHAFTS - R.R. FOR VERSIONS WITH AIR BAG

With the engine running and the vehicle stationary, the steering wheel oscillates and vibrates 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION First of all, check the engine idle speed Check the tyre pressure. Move on to Step 1 1. Engine idle irregular 1. Proceed as instructed in the See table D010 ENGINE IDLE IRREGULAR 2. Tyre inflation pressure not correct 2. Make sure tyres are inflated to the correct pressure. 1 ENGINE FLEXIBLE MOUNTINGS CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition and the centering of the engine frame, the engine flexible mountings and the engine side and gearbox side connecting rods. Move on to Step 2 1. Engine flexible mountings faulty. 1. Adjust the fastenings: loosen the bolts, centre them in their housings and tighten them to the recommended torque, see Assembly Op. 1008A POWER UNIT FASTENINGS 2. Engine side and gearbox side connecting rods faulty. 2. Adjust the fastenings: loosen the bolts, centre them in their housings and tighten them to the recommended torque, see Assembly Op. 1008C POWER UNIT REACTION ELEMENTS 3. Engine frame faulty. 3. Adjust the fastenings: loosen the bolts, centre them in their housings and tighten them to the recommended torque. Op. 4410D13 2 STEERING COLUMN CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the steering column support and that it is working properly. In particular, check: that there is no clearance between the support bushes and steering column; that the steering column joints are correctly tightened. Move on to Step 3 1. Bushes worn or damaged. 1. Restore the efficiency of the steering column. If necessary, replace the bearings involved Op. 4110A30 SUPPORT WITH STEERING CONTROL SHAFTS - R+R 2. Joint spider clearance too large. 2. Tighten the bolts or replace the steering column Op. 4110A30 SUPPORT WITH STEERING CONTROL SHAFTS - R+R 3 STEERING WHEEL ADJUSTMENT DEVICE CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the steering wheel adjustment device. In particular, check that the clearance between the device and the steering column is correct. Move on to Step 4 Coupling with excessive clearance. Restore the efficiency of the steering wheel adjustment device. Replace it if necessary. 4 TIMING CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the engine timing is correct. Move on to Step 5 Timing not correct. Restore correct engine timing Op. 1032B14 5 FLYWHEEL BALANCING CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the flywheel is correctly balanced. End of diagnosis Balancing not correct. Replace the flywheel Op. 1024B10 ENGINE FLYWHEEL - R + R FOR VERSIONS WITH MANUAL GEARBOX

When the key is inserted in the key recognition device the steering is not released. Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation First, check that: - The battery is run down (not below 8.5 Volt) - The key is recognized and that the Body asks for the release of the steering Move on to Step 1 Battery run down Recharge the battery Key not recognized/the Body does not ask for the release of the steering Replace the key with one that is recognized 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT All OK Problems encountered Operation Connect the diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket and check: - for the presence of possible errors at the Teg Reader node - for the presence of possible errors at the steering lock node - for the presence of possible errors at the B-Can Move on to Step 2 Teg Reader power supply not correct Restore correct power supply See E7065 ELECTRIC STEERING LOCK Presence of errors at the Teg-Reader Continue as described by the diagnostic equipment Presence of errors at the B-Can Continue as described by the diagnostic equipment 2 ELECTRICAL CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation Using the diagnostic equipment as a multimeter, check: - that the key recognition device is working properly See Test 5505AF CHECK OF THE EFFICIENCY OF KEY ACKNOWLEDGEMENT DEVICE - that the steering lock is working correctly See Test 5580ED ELECTRIC STEERING LOCK CHECK Move on to Step 3 3 STEERING LOCK OPERATION CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Using the diagnostic equipment, check in active diagnosis that the steering lock is working properly End of diagnosis Steering lock defective Replace the steering lock node Op. 5580E17 STEERING LOCK - R.R

The steering is not locked with the vehicle stationary and the key extracted Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation First of all check that none of the following conditions exists: . 5 seconds have not elapsed since the key was extracted . The same key or another object was inserted in the key recognition device within 5 seconds of the key being extracted . A key recovery extraction was carried out Move on to Step 1 5 seconds have not elapsed since the key was extracted Wait for 5 seconds The same key or another object was inserted in the key recognition device within 5 seconds of the key being extracted Do not reinsert the key or another object in the recognition device A key recovery extraction was carried out Proceed as instructed See table B006 KEY CANNOT BE EXTRACTED FROM BLOCK 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT All OK Problems encountered Operation Connect the diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket and check at the brake node that the data for the wheel speed is valid Move on to Step 2 Error detected for the wheel speed Continue as described by the diagnostic equipment 2 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT All OK Problems encountered Operation Connect the diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket and check the following at the steering lock node: - That there are no errors - Continuity of the wiring See E7065 ELECTRIC STEERING LOCK - B-Can continuity - Correct presence of signals at the steering lock See Test 5580ED ELECTRIC STEERING LOCK CHECK Move on to Step 3 Presence of errors Continue as described by the diagnostic equipment Wiring broken Restore wiring See E7065 ELECTRIC STEERING LOCK B-Can interrupted Restore B-Can continuity See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES Signals not correct Restore signals See E7065 ELECTRIC STEERING LOCK 3 STEERING LOCK OPERATION CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Using the diagnostic equipment, check in active diagnosis that the steering lock is working properly End of diagnosis Steering lock defective Replace steering lock node Op. 5580E17 STEERING LOCK - R.R

With the ignition ON, when the lever on the right of the steering wheel is operated, the windscreen wash/wipe does not work properly 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that neither the windscreen wipers nor the windscreen washer is working Move on to Step 1 1. With the ignition ON, when the lever on the right of the steering wheel is operated, the windscreen wipers do not work properly 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION With the panel off, lift up the wiper blades and check that the pins are correctly fastened to the arm holders. Move on to Step 2 The fuse is broken. Replace the fuse (and find out what could have caused it to blow). 2 VEHICLE WIRING CONNECTIONS CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Following the removal of the wiper arms and trim, check the condition of the vehicle wiring connector and make sure it is correctly inserted in the windscreen wiper socket. Op. 5050B34 WINDSCREEN WIPER ARM/S COMPLETE WITH BLADE - R+R Move on to Step 3 1.Connector damaged. 1. Replace the connector. 2.Connector not correctly inserted. 2. Restore correct connection. 3 CHECK ON TENSION AT WIRING TERMINALS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Disconnect the connector from the windscreen wiper and switch on the panel and select the various functions using the steering column switch unit checking the tension at the wiring terminals (correct tension at battery terminals 13.5 V). End of diagnosis 1. The voltage measured is not correct (the wiring is broken or the steering column switch unit is not working properly). 1. Restore the correct connections and/or replace the steering column switch unit. Op. 5050A12 WINDSCREEN WASHER FLUID RESERVOIR FILLER PIPE (IN ENGINE COMPARTMENT) - R.R. 2. The voltage measured is the same as that of the battery (windscreen wiper defective) 2. Move on to Step 4. 4 WINDSCREEN WIPER MOTOR POWER SUPPLY CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the following, in order: Connection to earth of motor; Motor power supply line See E3020 WINDSCREEN WASH/WIPE Move on to Step 5 Connection broken. Restore the correct connections. 5 WINDSCREEN WIPER MOTOR CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the windscreen wiper motor is working properly and, in particular, the internal electronic device. End of diagnosis 1.Motor intermittent electronic device faulty. 1. Replace the intermittent electronic device. Op. 5050B52 FRONT WINDSCREEN WIPER MOTOR INTERMITTENT FUNCTION - R R 2. Windscreen wiper motor faulty. 2. Replace the windscreen wiper motor. Op. 5050B42 WINDSCREEN WIPER MOTOR - R+R

With the ignition on, the display either does not show the time or it is not correct. 1 INSTRUMENT PANEL FUNCTIONS CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check: That the display shows the correct time That it is possible to adjust the time That the clock moves forward Move on to Step 2 1. Move on to Step 2 2 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket. With the ignition ON, the fuel reserve warning light does not come on when the tank is in the reserve condition The fuel level message is supplied by the "body computer node" and is made available to the "instrument panel node" via the B-CAN and to the gauge via a serial line. The "Body Computer node" also sends the fuel level sensor error message 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket. Check that there are no faults in the Body Computer Move on to Step 2 Sensor with broken circuit, sensor short circuited, value implausible/not consistent with actual fuel level Continue as described by the diagnostic equipment 2 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Keeping the Examiner equipment connected to the diagnostic socket, check the operation of the fuel reserve warning light in active diagnosis Move on to Step 3 1.The warning light does not come because the serial line is interrupted 1.Renew serial line 2.Instrument power supply interrupted 2.Restore power supply 3.Instrument defective 3.Replace instrument panel Op. 5560B10 CONTROL PANEL - R+R 3 CHECK FUEL LEVEL SENSOR ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check fuel level sensor operation by carrying out the Test See Test 1040AC FUEL LEVEL GAUGE CHECK Move on to Step 4 Sensor not working. Replace the fuel pump assembly Op. 1040A70 SUBMERGED PUMP ASSEMBLY COMPLETE WITH LEVEL GAUGE CONTROL - R + R 4 ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the continuity/insulation of the lead between fuel level sensor and Body Computer See E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL Move on to Step 5 Connections broken/not insulated Restore cable continuity/insulation 5 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis The fault persists Replace Body Computer Op. 5505A32 BODY COMPUTER - R.R

With the ignition on, the maximum engine coolant temperature gauge on the auxiliary instrument panel is not working The signal is made available to the instrument panel and via a serial line to the gauge. 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Keeping the Examiner connected to the diagnostic socket, check the operation of the pointer on the instrument panel by means of active diagnosis Move on to Step 2 The pointer does not operate because the instrument is defective Replace the gauge Op. 5560C51 COMBINED ANALOGUE CONTROL PANEL - R+R OR REPLACE 2 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket. Check for faults in the Engine Control Node Move on to Step 3 1. Serial line with NQS broken 1. Restore the serial line 2. Instrument panel power supply interrupted 2. Restore power supply 3.Instrument defective 3. Replace the gauge Op. 5560C51 COMBINED ANALOGUE CONTROL PANEL - R+R OR REPLACE 3 CHECK FOR ENGINE CONTROL FAULTS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION The panel indicates errors not detected by the engine control unit: proceed as instructed in the See table K101 MIL WARNING LIGHT STAYS ON (ENGINE STARTS) End of diagnosis ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the continuity/insulation of the cable between the engine coolant temperature sensor, engine control unit, Body Computer and instrument panel See E5030 PETROL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT 1.Leads broken/not insulated 1. Restore cable continuity/insulation 2. Temperature sensor defective 2.Replace the engine temperature sensor Op. 1060G14 ENGINE COOLANT TEMPERATURE SENSOR - R.R. 4 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present See E5030 PETROL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT End of diagnosis The fault persists. Replace Body Computer Op. 5505A32 BODY COMPUTER - R.R

With the ignition on, the engine coolant temperature gauge on the instrument panel is not working the engine temperature and the engine temperature sensor signal is made available by the "engine management node" via the C-CAN; the "body computer node" makes the message available on the B-CAN via the gateway and then to the instrument panel. 0 PRELIMINARY CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the engine control warning light does not come on with the engine started Move on to Step 2 Warning light on Move on to Step 1 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket. Check for faults in the Engine Control Node Move on to Step 2 Presence of faults Continue as described by the diagnostic equipment 2 CHECK FOR ENGINE CONTROL FAULTS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION The panel indicates errors not detected by the engine control unit: proceed as instructed in the See table K101 MIL WARNING LIGHT STAYS ON (ENGINE STARTS) End of diagnosis 3 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Keeping the Examiner connected to the diagnostic socket, check the operation of the warning light on the instrument panel by means of active diagnosis Move on to Step 4 1. The warning light does not come on for the serial line with the NQS interrupted 1. Move on to Step 4 2. Instrument power supply interrupted 2. Move on to Step 5 4 SERIAL LINE CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the continuity/insulation of the serial line between the auxiliary gauge and the instrument panel by peforming the Test See Test 5560BW CHECK AUXILIARY INSTRUMENTS Move on to Step 5 Serial line broken Restore the serial line 5 SUPPLY CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the auxiliary gauge is correctly supplied by conducting the Test See Test 5560BW CHECK AUXILIARY INSTRUMENTS Move on to Step 6 1. Power supply interrupted 1. Restore power supply 2. Auxiliary instrument defective 2. Replace the gauge Op. 5560C51 COMBINED ANALOGUE CONTROL PANEL - R+R OR REPLACE 6 ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the continuity/insulation of the cable between the engine coolant temperature sensor, engine control unit, Body Computer and instrument panel See E5030 PETROL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT Move on to Step 7 Connections broken/not insulated Restore cable continuity/insulation 7 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis The fault persists Replace Body Computer Op. 5505A32 BODY COMPUTER - R.R

After the initial test, the light check warning light on the Instrument Panel Node remains on. with the side light control active and with fault status for one of the rear bulbs, the NBC implements a recovery strategy: the brake light bulb on the corresponding side comes on in low power mode to simulate the brightness of a 5 W bulb 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Press the parking light activation button, move the steering wheel stalk and check the parking lights come on. Press the emergency light switch and check they activate correctly. Then turn the key ON and check the operation of the side lights/number plate lights. Activate the rear fog lamp from the control panel and check they operate correctly. Operate the side lights from the stalk and check they operate correctly Press the brake pedal and check the brake lights come on Move on to Step 1 1. Parking light bulb does not operate 1. Continue as instructed in the See table I002 PARKING LIGHTS NOT WORKING 2. Side light/number plate light bulb does not operate 2. Continue as instructed in the See table I001 SIDE LIGHTS/NO. PLATE LIGHTS NOT WORKING 3. Hazard light bulb does not operate 3. Continue as instructed in the See table I039 DIRECTION INDICATORS NOT WORKING WHEN HAZARD WARNING LIGHT SWITCH IS PRESSED 4. Turn signal does not operate 4. Continue as instructed in the See table I010 DIRECTION INDICATORS / HAZARD WARNING LIGHTS NOT WORKING 5. Rear fog lamp bulb does not operate 5. Continue as instructed in the See table I021 REAR FOG LAMPS NOT WORKING 6. Brake light bulb does not operate 6. Continue as instructed in the See table I014 BRAKE LIGHTS AND THIRD BRAKE LIGHT NOT WORKING 1 CHECK ELECTRICAL CONNECTIONS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the electrical connections between the Body Computer and the light wiring, in particular that each individual pin is correctly connected Move on to Step 2 Electrical connections defective Renew the damaged electrical connections 2 CHECK BULB POWER UPTAKE ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the light bulb power uptake is as specified Move on to Step 3 Bulbs of incorrect power rating or with defective filament Replace the bulbs 3 CHECK INSTRUMENT PANEL ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect an Examiner to check for errors in the instrument panel Move on to Step 4 Panel defective Replace the instrument panel Op. 5560B10 CONTROL PANEL - R+R 4 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis The fault persists Replace Body Computer Op. 5505A32 BODY COMPUTER - R.R

At the end of the check, the mileometer/trip counter on the panel begins to flash 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect an Examiner and check that the Instrument Panel Node is aligned in Control Unit Test, Other System Group and Proxy Alignment Procedure modes. With the key ON, the fuel consumption gauge on the display (one of the displays on the TRIP COMPUTER module) is not operational. N.B : The display provides two types of fuel consumption reading, instantaneous or average. The fuel consumption readings are processed by the instrument panel node on the basis of information received from the body computer node (mileage) and the engine control node (litre of fuel consumed) made availablet to the instrument panel node via the B-CAN and C-CAN networks respectively. In the absence of speed information (from the Brake Node) or instantaneous fuel consumption data (from the Engine Control Node), the fuel consumption data will be replaced by the reading "----" 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Interview the customer to check that the TRIP function have not been recently reset Move on to Step 1 One of the Trip Computer functions has been reset The display reading will be "----" until sufficient distance has been covered to allow fuel consumption to be evaluated: if the value is not displayed after a few kilometres, continue to Step 1 1 CAN NETWORK CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect an EXAMINER and check the following on CAN NETWORK INFORMATION: No control units inactive No faulty control units No control units with faulty CAN line Move on to Step 2 1. Fault on CAN network 1. Continue following the instructions for the diagnostic equipment 2. Communication impossible with the Body Computer 2. Move on to Step 9 2 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Keeping the diagnostic instrument connected, check the following on the BRAKE NODE: No system/component errors No CAN faults Move on to Step 3 1. System/components faulty 1. Continue following the instructions for the diagnostic equipment 2. Fault on C-CAN network 2. Move on to Step 11 3 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Keeping the diagnostic instrument connected, check the following on the ENGINE CONTROL NODE: No system/component errors No CAN faults Move on to Step 4 1. System/components faulty 1. Continue following the instructions for the diagnostic equipment 2. Fault on C-CAN network 2. Move on to Step 11 4 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Keeping the diagnostic instrument connected, check the following on the INSTRUMENT PANEL NODE: No system/component errors No CAN faults Move on to Step 5 1. System/components faulty 1. Continue following the instructions for the diagnostic equipment 2. Fault on C-CAN network 2. Move on to Step 11 5 ACTIVE DIAGNOSIS CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION With the Examiner in Instrument Panel Node mode check that all segments of the LCD module are correctly activated in Active Diagnosis. Move on to Step 8 1. One or more segments does not activate 1. Replace the instrument panel Op. 5560B10 CONTROL PANEL - R+R 2. Communication impossible with the instrument panel 2. Move on to Step 6 6 ELECTRICAL POWER SUPPLY CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the Instrument Panel Node elecricity supply is correct Move on to Step 7 Fault in positive electricity supply and/or earth Replace defective component (in the case of a fuse, find out what caused it to blow). 7 CHECK ELECTRICAL CONNECTIONS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the electrical connections between the Body Computer and the Instrument Panel, in particular that each individual pin is correctly connected Move on to Step 8 Electrical connections not operating Renew the damaged electrical connections 8 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Using the Examiner in Body Computer mode, check that the following errors are not present: Move on to Step 12 1. Impossible to connect to the Body Computer control unit. 1. Move on to Step 9 2. Presence of errors 2. Continue by following the instructions on the diagnostic instrument 9 ELECTRICAL POWER SUPPLY CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the Body Computer Node elecricity supply is correct Move on to Step 10 Fault in positive electricity supply and/or earth Replace defective component (in the case of a fuse, find out what caused it to blow). 10 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Use an Examiner to check the possibility of connecting to the Body Computer Node Move on to Step 11 Impossible to connect to the Body Computer control unit. Replace Body Computer Op. 5505A32 BODY COMPUTER - R.R 11 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis

The Engine Management node sends a message via the C-CAN network to the Body Computer, which makes it available to the Instrument Panel Node via the B-CAN network. Any faults in the C-CAN network turn on the warning lights of the control units that communicate on this network. The CAN Network Information check is intended to detect this situation. 1 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect an Examiner and check on CAN Network Information for the absence of: Inactive node/s Node/s with error/s Node/s with CAN network fault Move on to Step 6 1. Engine Control Node inactive and/or with error 1. Continue as instructed by the diagnostic equipment 2. Fault in CAN network 2. Continue as instructed by the diagnostic equipment 2 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Use an Examiner to check the possibility of connection to the Body Computer Node, the lack of errors and the presenc of parameters Move on to Step 3 Presence of errors Continue as instructed by the diagnostic equipment 3 ACTIVE DIAGNOSIS CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION With the Examiner in Instrument Panel Node mode, check that the minimum oil pressure warning light is correctly activated in Active Diagnosis. Move on to Step 4 1. The warning light does not flash 1. Replace the instrument panel Op. 5560B10 CONTROL PANEL - R+R 2. The warning light flashes 2.Continue to step 4 4 OIL PRESSURE SENSOR CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check correct operation of the oil pressure sensor Move on to Step 5 1. Pressure sensor defective 1. Replace pressure sensor Op. 1084A40 ENGINE OIL LEVEL SENSOR - R + R 2. Oil circuit pressure incorrect 2.Restore the correct pressure 3. Sensor wiring defective 3.Renew the wiring 5 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Using the Examiner diagnostic equipment check, in Engine Control Node mode, that there are no errors and that the parameters are present. Move on to Step 6 Fault persists Replace the Engine Management Control Unit Op. 1056B82 INJECTION/IGNITION SYSTEM E.C.U. (ONE) - R + R 5 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Using the Examiner diagnostic equipment check, in Engine Control Node mode, that there are no errors and that the parameters are present. Move on to Step 6 fault persists Replace the Engine Management Control Unit Op. 1060G80 DIESEL ELECTRONIC INJECTION CONTROL UNIT - .R 6 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis

The engine fault warning light flashes with the engine started The warning light can flash in two different ways: with the engine started up and the vehicle stationary or with the vehicle driving. 1 FUEL RESERVE WARNING LIGHT CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fuel reserve warning light is off Move on to Step 2 Fuel reserve warning light on Top up the fuel level so that it is not in the reserve zone and continue to Step 4 2 FUEL LEVEL CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fuel level gauge is working properly Move on to Step 3 Fuel level gauge not working Proceed as instructed in the See table K020 FUEL LEVEL GAUGE NOT WORKING 3 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the diagnostic instrument (Examiner or Examiner Plus) and check the absence of the Misfiring error End of diagnosis The "misfire" error is present Proceed as instructed in the See table Z53 MISFIRE ERROR 4 ERROR CANCELLING AND CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Using the diagnostic equipment, cancel the errors in the control unit. When the belt is fastened and with the vehicle parked, the belt locks easily and/or remains locked even when movements are not abrupt (e.g. picking up an object) 1 CHECK REEL ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the reel is correctly fitted, ensuring that the reference pin is correctly positioned in its seat on the vehicle body. When the relevant control is operated, the sunroof opens/closes irregularly, locking at certain points or remaining stuck at an angle. 1 CHECK SUNROOF DEVICES ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Remove the glass panel Op. 7030B18 SLIDING ROOF GLASS PANEL - R+R Check the operation of the sunroof operating devices. Restore the feed mechanism Op. 7030B50 SUN ROOF SLIDING GUIDE (ONE), LH OR RH - R.R 2 CHECK SUNROOF CONTROL DEVICES ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Remove the motor Op. 7030B70 SUN ROOF MOVEMENT MOTOR - R+R Check the operation of the sunroof operating devices. Replace the end of travel buffer. 4 END OF TRAVEL BUFFER CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the end of travel buffer is correctly inserted in its housing by carrying out the Test 4410AA Move on to Step 5 End of travel buffer not correctly inserted Refit the buffer correctly 5 CHECKS UNDER THE FLOOR All OK Problems encountered Operation Position the vehicle on a two column lift and raise it. Replace the connecting rod. Creaking of the bar centre flexible mountings during manual movement with a symmetrical load applied. Replace the anti-roll bar Op. 4410C10 FRONT SUSPENSION ANTI-ROLL BAR - R+R - CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY 8 LOWER TRACK CONTROL ARM THRUST BUSHES CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check, by placing a sheet of paper between the crossmember and the rear bush, that there is no interference in the contact area between the rubber and the thrust washers If the spring shows signs of abrasion, its mechanical properties could be weakened as a result of oxidation End of diagnosis Creaking at the rear bush. Whilst driving, especially on unmade roads, there is knocking coming from the front suspension. This diagnosis can only be made after See table . Carry out the latter first.
