The noise occurs whilst accelerating or braking with the wheels steered. Move on to Step 3 The noise only occurs during acceleration or braking Move on to Step 1 The noise appears whilst braking when the road is slightly uneven Move on to Step 3 The noise is also present in other conditions Move on to Step 1 1 OIL LEAKS CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Raise the vehicle on a two column lift and check that there are no oil leaks from the shock absorber stem Slight dampness on the stem is considered normal because there is evaporation during the operation of the shock absorber. If there is a persistent oil leak on the shock absorber stem, make sure that it is not coming from other parts of the vehicle that are lubricated Move on to Step 2 Leaks from other parts that are lubricated Search for the cause of the leak following the appropriate diagnostic procedure Leaks from the shock absorber stem Replace the shock absorber Op. 4410A12 FRONT SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMANTLING/REASSEMBLY OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R 2 INTERFERENCE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there are no signs of interference between the suspension elements or between the latter and the bodyshell. Check that there are no signs of interference between the lower end of the shock absorber bar connecting rod and the front fastening for the crossmember. Also check that there are no signs of interference between the lower track control arm and the lower fork. In particular, check that there are no signs of wear on the suspension springs and that they do not show signs of abrasion. If the spring shows signs of abrasion, its mechanical properties could be weakened as a result of oxidation Move on to Step 3 Inteference due to incorrect fitting Eliminate the interference and restore the correct fastening. If this is not possible, replace the defective components Abrasions or non conformity of the spring Replace the spring Op. 4410A12 FRONT SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMANTLING/REASSEMBLY OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R taking care to fit it correctly Signs of interference between the lower end of the connecting rod and the crossmember front fastening Place a washer no larger than 3 mm between the connecting rod and the bar. Signs of interference between the lower track control arm and the lower fork Replace the lower track control arm 3 TIGHTENING TORQUE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Locate the area of the possible noise source: top or bottom. Starting from the area where the knocking was identified, check See Test See Test 4410OA CHECKING CORRECT TIGHTENING OF FRONT SUSPENSION The tightening torques of the fixing bolts for: upper shock absorber fastening to aluminium fork; upper shock absorber fastening to aluminium fork; anti-roll bar to crossmember fastening; fastening of lower/upper end of connecting rods for shock absorber anti-roll bar; inner/outer fastening for front/rear bushes for lower track control arms to crossmember; fastening of upper aluminium fork to bodyshell; fastening for upper track control arm to aluminium fork and steering knuckle; fastening between power assisted steering box rod and steering knuckle; fastening for steering box to crossmember; front/centre/rear fastening between crossmember and bodyshell; brake caliper fastening to steering knuckle; disc shield fastening. Also check that the anti-slip adhesive band is present where the crossmember is attached to the bodyshell in the middle and at the back Move on to Step 4 Torque tightenings not correct Restore the correct tightness Adhesive band not present Fit the anti-slip adhesive band 4 ANTI-ROLL BAR CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation After having disconnected the upper track rod end for the shock absorber connecting rod, check that the anti-roll bar does not rotate freely around the U-bolts securing it to the crossmember. After having disconnected the connecting rod, check that the clearance for the joints is not too large. Move on to Step 5 The anti-roll bar turns freely around the U-bolts securing it to the crossmember. Replace the anti-roll bar Connecting rod joints clearance too great. Replace the connecting rod. 5 UPPER TRACK CONTROL ARMS CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there is no clearance between the track control arm track rod ends and make sure that the boot is intact. The bolt connecting the track control arm to the steering knuckle must be loosened in order to carry out this operation. Also check the condition of the bushes. Move on to Step 6 There is clearance or the boot or the bushes are not intact. Replace the upper track control arm 7 LOWER TRACK CONTROL ARMS CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there are no glycol leaks from or signs of damage to the arm rear bush. Check that the track rod end clearance is not too large. In order to do so the guard under the engine must be removed Op. 7055B64 ENGINE COMPARTMENT DUST PROTECTION IN FRONT WHEEL ARCH LINER (ONE) LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R. and disconnect the bolt connecting it to the front steering knuckle Op. 4410B40 LOWER TRACK CONTROL ARM (WITH BALLJOINT) FOR LEFT OR RIGHT FRONT SUSPENSION (ONE) - R+R - CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY Also check the condition of the front bushes. If the spring shows signs of abrasion, its mechanical properties could be weakened as a result of oxidation Move on to Step 8 Glycol leak from the rear bush Replace the lower track control arm There is clearance or the boot or the bushes are not intact Replace the lower track control arm 6 SPRING/SHOCK ABSORBER ASSEMBLY CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the presence and condition of the rubber support seals for the upper/lower spring. The shock absorber must be removed in order to carry out this operation Op. 4410A10 L/H OR R/H FRONT SUSPENSION SPRING/DAMPER UNIT (ONE) - R+R - CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY IF NECESSARY checking that the stem projects evenly after the application of manual compression. Move on to Step 7 Upper/lower rubber seals not intact. Replace the rubber seals Stem reascendence irregular. Replace the shock absorber Op. 4410A10 L/H OR R/H FRONT SUSPENSION SPRING/DAMPER UNIT (ONE) - R+R - CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY IF NECESSARY 8 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis The fault persists The fault is due to another system (engine, clutch, differential). Search for the cause in one of these systems, following the appropriate diagnostic procedures

Replace the wheel side constant velocity joint Op. 2710A20 WHEEL SIDE CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT (ONE), L/H OR R/H - R + R WITH DRIVESHAFT REMOVED - INCLUDES BOOT REPLACEMENT and carry out the correct greasing. 5 WHEEL SIDE JOINT TIGHTENING CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Remove the left wheel Op. 4450B02 LEFT FRONT WHEEL - R.R and/or the right one Op. 4450B04 RIGHT FRONT WHEEL - R.R Check that the constant velocity joint fastening nut is tightened and that the staking is in place. With the engine running, there is noise at take off when the various gears are engaged: the noise changes as the speed changes. Results of the tests 1 REDUCTION GEAR CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the reduction gear More specifically: - it should not be worn or damaged; - there should not be excessive clearance; - the ring gear fastenings should not be slack. Move on to Step 2 Reduction gear damaged Restore the clearance or, if necessary, replace the reduction gear 2 SATELLITE CARRIER PIN CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the wear of the satellite carrier pin or the housing in the differential casing Op. 2110D20 DIFFERENTIAL INTERNAL CASING, REMOVED - DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY, CHECK PLANET AND SATELLITE GEARS End of diagnosis Differential casing wear Replace the differential casing Op. 2110D10 DIFFERENTIAL INTERNAL CASING - R + R WITH MANUAL GEARBOX REMOVED - INCLUDES GEARBOX DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY

With the vehicle stationary, the gearbox in neutral and the engine running, there is a high frequency, low intensity noise coming from the area of the gearbox. Press the clutch pedal and check whether the noise increases. Check the gearbox/differential oil level Op. 0010T41 MANUAL GEARBOX OIL CHECK LEVEL AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY Move on to Step 1 Oil leak detected from the gearbox Proceed as instructed in the See table X15 GEARBOX/DIFFERENTIAL OIL LEAKS The noise disappears or decreases considerably with the clutch pedal pressed: the noise comes from inside the gearbox Proceed as instructed in the See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING Oil level too low. Restore the correct level Op. 0010T41 MANUAL GEARBOX OIL CHECK LEVEL AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY and carry out a road test. If the fault persists, move on to Step 1 1 SPLINED HUB CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check for excess grease on the clutch plate hub bushes and the gearbox main shaft Move on to Step 2 Gearbox main shaft hub faulty Replace the gearbox main shaft Op. 2110B MANUAL GEARBOX WITH DIFFERENTIAL GEARS AND SYNCHRONISERS Clutch plate hub bushes faulty. Restore the correct lubrication for the bushes. If necessary, replace the clutch plate Op. 1810A20 CLUTCH - R + R 2 CLUTCH PLATE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check: - Clutch plate wear; - Fouling (oil or grease) of the clutch plate; - That there is no distortion of the clutch plate; - That there is no damage to the pressure plate diaphragm spring. End of diagnosis Clutch plate or pressure plate faulty Replace the clutch plate Op. 1810A20 CLUTCH - R + R Presence of oil or grease. Also replace the gearbox input oil seal Op. 2110C22 GEAR INPUT SHAFT SEALS - R R

Move on to Step 2 Seals worn Replace the synchronizers Op. 2110B20 MANUAL GEARBOX (5-6SPEED) WITH DIFFERENTIAL - DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY - WASH AND CHECK PARTS - REPLACE SYNCHRONISERS AND INTERNAL CONTROLS IF NECESSARY 2 GEAR CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Overhaul the gearbox Op. 2110B20 In particular, check the teeth of the gear engaged: there should be no signs of wear or seizing Move on to Step 3 Gears worn Replace the gears involved Op. 2110B20 3 REDUCTION GEAR CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the reduction gear More specifically: - it should not be worn or damaged; - there should not be excessive clearance End of diagnosis Reduction gear damaged Restore the clearance or, if necessary, replace the reduction gear

If the noise persists, replace the shock absorber Op. 4410A12 FRONT SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMANTLING/REASSEMBLY OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R

Whilst driving, especially on unmade roads, there is knocking coming from the rear suspension. This diagnosis can only be made after See table . Carry out the latter first. If the problem is only on one side, carry out the checks and any operations on the appropriate side only. Results of the tests 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation Having carried out the road test, see the Table S15 RUMOROSITA'' in condizioni di marcia , there was a knocking noise from the back. Continue depending on the circumstances in which the noise occurs End of diagnosis The noise disappears when the handbrake is operated Restore the correct tightening of the rear brake calipers to the stub axle. The noise only occurs during acceleration or braking. Move on to Step 1 The noise is also present in other conditions. Move on to Step 1 1 OIL LEAKS CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Raise the vehicle on a two column lift and check that there are no oil leaks from the shock absorber stem. Slight dampness on the stem is considered normal because there is evaporation during the operation of the shock absorber. If there is a persistent oil leak on the shock absorber stem, make sure that it is not coming from other parts of the vehicle that are lubricated Move on to Step 2 Leaks from other parts that are lubricated Search for the cause of the leak following the appropriate diagnostic procedure Leaks from the shock absorber stem. Replace the shock absorber Op. Op. 4420A12 REAR SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMENTLING/REBUILDING OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH R R 2 HANDBRAKE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the handbrake cables or outer casing do not knock against the fuel tank, heat shields or bodywork during oscillations. Move on to Step 3 Inteference between outer casing or cables and other elements Cover the outer casing with foam rubber tape in the area of the interference or lubricate the cable 3 INTERFERENCE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there are no signs of interference between the suspension elements or between the latter and the bodyshell. In particular, check that there are no signs of wear on the suspension springs and that they do not show signs of abrasion Move on to Step 4 Inteference due to incorrect fitting Eliminate the interference and restore the correct fastening. If this is not possible, replace the defective components Abrasions or non conformity of the spring Replace the spring Op. Op. 4420A12 REAR SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMENTLING/REBUILDING OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH R R taking care to fit it correctly 4 TIGHTENING TORQUE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Locate the area of the possible noise source: top or bottom. Starting from the area where the knocking was identified, check the tightening torques See Test 4420B Verifiche corretti serraggi sospensioni posteriori Of the bolts fixing: longitudinal anchorage strut bushes to the hub; longitudinal anchorage strut bushes to the bodyshell; bushes for front/rear track control arms to the shock absorber; bushes for front/rear track control arms to the crossmember; shock absorber to steering knuckle lower fastenings; brake caliper to steering knuckle fastenings; brake disc shield fastenings; anti-roll bar to crossmember fastenings; crossmember to bodyshell fastenings; stub axle to hub upper/lower fastenings. connecting rod between anti-roll bar and shock absorber fastenings. Move on to Step 5 Torque tightenings not correct Restore the correct tightness 5 CHECK ON FRONT AND REAR TRACK CONTROL ARMS All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there is no clearance between the front and rear track control arms and the crossmember. Also check the condition of the suspension bushes. Move on to Step 6 There is clearance or the front arm bushes are not intact. Replace the front track control arms There is clearance or the rear arm bushes are not intact. Replace the rear track control arms 6 CHECK ON LONGITUDINAL ANCHORAGE STRUT All OK Problems encountered Operation Removing the protection for the fastening on the bodyshell side for the longitudinal anchorage strut Check that: there is no clearance between the anchorage strut and the bodyshell; there are no glycol leaks from the bush secured to the bodyshell; the rubber part of the bush, on the fastening securing the strut to the hub, is not detached from the steel outer casing. Move on to Step 7 There is clearance. Replace the anchorage strut Glycol leaks from the bodyshell side strut fastening bush. Replace the anchorage strut Rubber part of the bush detached from the steel outer casing. Replace the bush with a new one which has an aluminium outer casing (as described in Service News 44.03.04) 7 ANTI-ROLL BAR CONNECTING ROD CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there are no signs of wear or tears on the connecting rod boots. Move on to Step 8 Signs of wear or tears on the connecting rod boots. Replace the connecting rod 8 SHOCK ABSORBER UPPER MOUNTING TIGHTENING TORQUE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation When the luggage compartment interior lining side panels are removed following the Op. 7040B06 Check the tightening torques for the following bolts: shock absorber to turret upper fastening; damping plate to shock absorber fastening. Move on to Step 9 Torque tightenings not correct Restore the correct tightness 9 CHECK ON CONDITION OF SHOCK ABSORBER TO TURRET MOUNTING All OK Problems encountered Operation The shock absorber must be removed in order to carry out this check Op. 4420A10 L/H OR R/H REAR SUSPENSION SPRING/DAMPER UNIT (ONE) R+R , then check the condition of the shock absorber mounting on the turret. Move on to Step 10 Rubber detached from the metal parts of the mounting. Replace the mounting. 10 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the fault is no longer present. End of diagnosis The fault persists The knocking is caused by another system (e.g. the fuel float in the tank). Carry out the appropriate checks to identify the cause of the noise.

During a braking manoeuvre, whistling or squeaking can be heard from the wheel area. Vibrations are also felt in the passenger compartment 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Steer to the right or to the left and check whether the noise increases. Move on to Step 1 The noise changes during steering. Proceed as instructed in the See table S45 NOISE FROM FRONT / ROUND BENDS 1 CHECK THE PAD TYPE AND SURFACE ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check: intactness of the pad braking surfaces; pad type. Move on to Step 2 1. Front braking surfaces vitrified or with traces of grease, oil or water. Pads of non-specified type. 1. Re-clean, check and remove the fault causes. Replace the pads if necessary Op. 3310A60 FRONT BRAKE PADS - REPLACE 2. Rear braking surfaces vitrified or with traces of grease, oil or water. Pads of non-specified type. 2. Re-clean, check and remove the fault causes. Replace the pads if necessary Op. 3310B62 REAR BRAKE PADS - REPLACE 2 CHECK DISCS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the intactness of the brake discs. End of diagnosis 1. Front discs worn or damaged. Pads of non-specified type. 1. Regrind the discs or, if necessary, replace them Op. 3310A54 Op. 3310A52 2. Rear discs worn or damaged. Pads of non-specified type. 2. Regrind the discs or, if necessary, replace them Op. 3310B54 Op. 3310B52

When the brake pedal is depressed slightly (even with the brakes cold) at average speed, the steering wheel and the brake pedal vibrate. 1 CHECK THE WHEEL STUD TIGHTENING ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the wheel studs are correctly fastened Move on to Step 2 Incorrect tightness Tighten the wheel studs correctly. 2 CHECK FRONT DISCS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the following, in order: condition; changes in thickness; irregular disc wear. Move on to Step 3 Front discs worn irregularly or damaged. Regrind the discs or, if necessary, replace them Op. 3310A54 Op. 3310A52 3 CHECK ON PAD SURFACES CONDITION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check: pad brake surface intactness; that the pads are not worn. End of diagnosis 1. Brake surfaces vitrified or with traces of grease, oil or water 1. Clean again, check and remove the causes of the fault 2. Front pads worn (reduced pad compressibility) 2. Replace the front pads Op. 3310A60 FRONT BRAKE PADS - REPLACE

Whilst the steering is operated there is a noise when it reaches the end of travel position. 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Visually inspect the level of the power assisted steering fluid in the reservoir. Conduct a test by steering completely to one side and then releasing the steering wheel Move on to Step 1 1. Fluid level too low. 1. Restore the correct fluid level: if there are leaks, continue follow the instructions in See table X030 POWER ASSISTED STEERING SYSTEM FLUID LEAKS 2. The noise increases towards the end of travel position and with the engine speed (roar) 2. Move on to Step 1 3. The noise remains constant (hissing whilst steering, puffing on release) 3. No intervention is nececssary: the noise is due to the by-pass valve that discharges the excess pressure 1 CHECK ON POWER ASSISTED STEERING FLUID QUALITY ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Visually inspect the power assisted steering fluid in the reservoir. Make sure that there is no emulsified fluid (fluid that is lighter in colour with bubbles) Move on to Step 2 Emulsified fluid. Eliminate any air infiltration from the power assisted steering system pipes Op. 4130B10 POWER STEERING FLUID RESEVOIR - R.R. 2 POWER ASSISTED STEERING PIPES CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check for constrictions in the flexible and rigid system pipes. Move on to Step 3 Pipes faulty. Replace the damaged parts, replacing all the gaskets. See Assembly Op. 4130B POWER STEERING HYDRAULIC SYTEM 3 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION OF THE POWER STEERING PUMP ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the power assisted steering pump is working properly End of diagnosis Power assisted steering pump malfunction Replace the power assisted steering pump Op. 4130B24

After operating the steering numerous times, a noise is heard when the steering wheel is left still 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Visually inspect the level of the power assisted steering fluid in the reservoir. Conduct a test by steering completely to one side and then releasing the steering wheel Move on to Step 1 1. Fluid level too low. 1. Restore the correct fluid level: if there are leaks, continue follow the instructions in See table X030 POWER ASSISTED STEERING SYSTEM FLUID LEAKS 2. The noise heard is a knock/striking noise 2. Move on to Step 1 3. A blowing noise is heard in correspondence with the three steering wheel positions (120° apart) 3. No intervention is nececssary: the noise is due to the by-pass valve that discharges the excess pressure 1 CHECK STEERING COLUMN BEARINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check for excessive play in the steering column: check the condition and efficiency of the steering column mount bearings. End of diagnosis Bearings worn or damaged Replace the affected bearings Op. 4110A30 SUPPORT WITH STEERING CONTROL SHAFTS - R+R

Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the following, in order: - engine idle speed - that the tyres are the correct type, in good condition and correctly inflated - correct tightening of wheel bolts Move on to Step 1 Engine idle irregular Proceed as instructed by the See table D010 ENGINE IDLE IRREGULAR Tyre inflation pressure not correct Restore the correct tyre inflation pressure Tyres unsuitable or worn Replace the tyres Wheel bolts not correctly tightened Tighten the wheel studs correctly 1 WHEEL CHECK Check: All OK Problems encountered Operation - that the wheels are correctly balanced - the condition of the wheel rims (they should not show signs of dents or distortions) Move on to Step 2 Wheels not balanced Balance the wheels correctly Wheel rims dented or distorted Replace the wheel rims 2 ENGINE FLEXIBLE MOUNTINGS CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the condition and the centering of the engine frame, the engine flexible mountings and the engine side and gearbox side connecting rods Move on to Step 3 Engine flexible mountings faulty Adjust the fastenings: loosen the bolts, centre them in their housings and tighten them to the recommended torque. Op. 1008A POWER UNIT FASTENINGS Engine side and gearbox side connecting rods faulty Adjust the fastenings: loosen the bolts, centre them in their housings and tighten them to the recommended torque. Op. 1008C POWER UNIT REACTION ELEMENTS Engine frame faulty Adjust the fastenings: loosen the bolts, centre them in their housings and tighten them to the recommended torque. Op. 4410D10 FRONT SUSPENSION FRAME - R+R 3 STEERING COLUMN CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the condition of the steering column support and that it is working properly. In particular, check: - that there is no clearance between the support bushes and steering column - that the steering column joints are correctly tightened - the condition of the steering column supports and that they are working properly Move on to Step 4 Bushes worn or damaged Restore the efficiency of the steering column. If necessary, replace the bearings involved Op. 4110A30 SUPPORT WITH STEERING CONTROL SHAFTS - R+R Joint spider clearance too large Tighten the bolts or replace the steering column Op. 4110A30 SUPPORT WITH STEERING CONTROL SHAFTS - R+R Bearings worn or damaged Restore the efficiency of the steering column. If necessary, replace the bearings involved 4 CHECK ON CONDITION OF FLEXIBLE MOUNTINGS AND BUSHES All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the condition of the bushes and mountings. In the following order: - ball joints for steering box rods - bushes for upper and lower track control arms - anti-roll bar flexible mountings Move on to Step 5 Steering box rod ball joints worn or damaged Replace the rods Op. 4110B10 STEERING LINKS - R+R ON VEHICLE - CHECK TOE-IN/TOE-OUT SEPARATELY Bushes for upper or lower arms worn or damaged Replace the upper track control arms Op. 4410B68 LOWER SWINGING ARM(ONE), LH OR RH OF FRONT SUSPENSION - R R -CHECK WHEEL ALIGNMENT SEPARATELY or the lower track control arms Op. 4410B40 LOWER TRACK CONTROL ARM (WITH BALLJOINT) FOR LEFT OR RIGHT FRONT SUSPENSION (ONE) - R+R - CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY Anti-roll bar mountings Replace the flexible mountings for anti-roll bar Op. 4410C12 FRONT SUSPENSION ANTI ROLL BAR JOINT (END) (ONE), LH OR RH - R.R 5 SPRING SHOCK ABSORBER ASSEMBLY CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check: - the condition of the shock absorbers and the springs and that they are working efficiently - the fastenings of the spring/shock absorber assembly Move on to Step 6 Tightening not correct Renew the correct fastening Shock abosrbers not working properly Replace the shock absorber involved Op. 4410A12 FRONT SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMANTLING/REASSEMBLY OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R Springs not working properly Replace the spring involved Op. 4410A12 FRONT SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMANTLING/REASSEMBLY OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R 6 STEERING RODS AND ARMS CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the condition of the steering rods and arms Move on to Step 7 Rods damaged or worn Replace the rods Op. 4110B10 STEERING LINKS - R+R ON VEHICLE - CHECK TOE-IN/TOE-OUT SEPARATELY Arms damaged or worn Replace the steering box Op. 4130A15 POWER STEERING BOX R R WITH FRONT SUSPENSION FRAME REMOVED 7 INTERMEDIATE SHAFT DAMPER CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the intermediate shaft torsion damper is working properly Move on to Step 8 Torsion damper not working properly Replace the intermediate shaft 8 STEERING WHEEL ADJUSTMENT DEVICE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the condition of the steering wheel adjustment device In particular, check that the clearance between the device and the steering column is correct Move on to Step 4 Coupling with excessive clearance Restore the efficiency of the steering wheel adjustment device. If necessary, replace it 9 TIMING CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the engine timing is correct Move on to Step 5 Timing not correct Restore correct engine timing 10 FLYWHEEL BALANCING CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the flywheel is correctly balanced End of diagnosis Balancing not correct Replace the flywheel Op. 1024B10 ENGINE FLYWHEEL - R + R FOR VERSIONS WITH MANUAL GEARBOX

0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the climate control system to the special repressurizing equipment and check the system pressures by carrying out the See Test 5040OB Air conditioning system operational check (pressure) Check the wear condition and correct belt alignment and tensioning. Run the engine at idle speed with the A/C system off and check whether the noise comes from other auxiliary components (engine fan, water pump, alternator). Increase the rpm and check for vibrations. Move on to Step 2 1. Pressure level incorrect 1. Move on to Step 1 2. Belt alignment/tension incorrect or belt worn. 2. Restore correct alignment/tension or replace the belt. 3. The noise is from other auxiliary components (engine cooling fan, coolant pump, alternator). 3. Continue as indicated in the diagnostic test procedure. 1 CHECK PRESSURE VALUES IN HIGH AND LOW PRESSURE CIRCUIT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Keep the recharging device connected and check the pressure levels in the system high and low pressure circuit with the compressor on and engine running: pressure values low in high and low pressure circuit; pressure values high in high and low pressure circuit; check that the pressure values (high and low) during compressor operation do not pulse and that the circuit does not equalise slowly when the engine is turned off. End of diagnosis 1. Low circuit pressure values (insufficient coolant in circuit) 1. Flush the system and restore the correct charge of fluid and gas Op. 0010T84 COOLANT FOR AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM - DEHYDRATE AND REPRESSURIZE 2. High circuit pressure values (too much coolant in circuit) 2. Flush the system and restore the correct charge of fluid and gas Op. 0010T84 COOLANT FOR AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM - DEHYDRATE AND REPRESSURIZE 3. Pulsing circuit pressure values (compressor discharge valve permanently open) 3. Replace the compressor Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY If the compressor is replaced due to a mechanical problem, remember to clean the entire circuit and change the drier filter. 2 CHECK ON FASTENING OF PIPES AND COMPONENTS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the compressor, the pipes and the system components are correctly fastened. Check the following, in order: bracket fastening to the engine block; fastening of pipes (by bands and spacers) no interference between pipes and other components in the engine compartment; condenser cleanlineness or damage (presence of mud, foreign bodies). Also check for cracks in the compressor fastenings to the bracket on the engine block. Move on to Step 3 1. Fastening of components incorrect 1. Retighten fastenings to torque 2. Interference in the engine compartment 2. Restore the correct layout of the pipes 3. Condenser obstructed or damaged. 3. Clean or replace the condenser Op. 5040A40 AIR CONDITIONING CONDENSER - R+R 4. Also check for cracks in the compressor fastenings to the bracket on the engine block. 4. Replace the compressor Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY 3 CHECKS TO CARRIED OUT WITHOUT THE COMPRESSOR ON ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Checks to be carried out without the compressor on: disconnect the service belt and check for contact between the armature and pulley; with the belt disconnected, check for contact between the pulley and external elements. check the wear of the pulley bearing by rotating the moving plate in both directions of rotation. check whether the compressor magnetic coupling shows signs of overheating. Move on to Step 4 1. Presence of contact between armature and pulley. 1. Replace the compressor electromagnetic coupling with pulley Op. 5040A34 PULLEY WITH COMPRESSOR ELECTROMAGNETIC COUPLING - R+R WITH COMPRESSOR REMOVED 2. Presence of contact between the pulley and external elements. 2. Remove the contact. 3. Bearing worn 3. Replace the pulley Op. 5040A34 PULLEY WITH COMPRESSOR ELECTROMAGNETIC COUPLING - R+R WITH COMPRESSOR REMOVED 4. Signs of overheating on the compressor magnetic coupling 4. Replace the pulley Op. 5040A34 PULLEY WITH COMPRESSOR ELECTROMAGNETIC COUPLING - R+R WITH COMPRESSOR REMOVED If the compressor is replaced due to a mechanical problem, remember to clean the entire circuit and change the drier filter. 4 CHECKS TO CARRIED OUT WITH THE COMPRESSOR ON ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION After restoring the correct connection of the service belt, turn the compressor on and off to check: visually if the compressor magnetic coupling plate slips due to oil or grease on the plate; if slippage takes place between the compressor belt and pulley. Move on to Step 5 1. Oil or grease on the plate. 1. Clean the oil or grease off the plate and find the oil leak. 2. Slippage between compressor belt and pulley. 2. Replace the belt 5 CHECK FOR GAS LEAKS ON THE COMPRESSOR SIDE ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION With the engine started and the climate control system at the maximum speed (compressor button ON), place the temperature adjustment knob/button in the maximum cold position, move the probe of the leak detector near the connector to be analyzed and check for any leaks. If there is a leak, repeat the test to make sure that there really is a leak. Withdraw the pipes from the compressor and ensure that the o-rings on the pipes are correctly positioned. Check the condition of the pipe fastening threads on the compressor. With the engine off and the compressor off, bring the leak detector probe up to the compressor pulley near the shaft stem and rear cylinder head gasket to check for leaks. If there is a leak, repeat the test to make sure that there really is a leak. Also check whether the leak is located in other coolant system components. End of diagnosis 1. Compressor pipe o-rings poorly positioned (pinching). 1. Reposition the compressor pipe o-rings correctly. 2. Pipe fastening threads not intact. 2. Replace the compressor Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY 3. Leak located on shaft stem or compressor rear head. 3. Replace the compressor Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY 4. Leak located in other cooling system components. 4. Remove the leak and restore the circuit to correct operation. If the compressor is replaced due to a mechanical problem, remember to clean the entire circuit and change the drier filter.

Whilst driving there is noise coming from the fan. This diagnosis can only be made after See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING Carry out the latter first. The climate control is working normally but there is excessive noise coming from the passenger compartment fan. 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Having carried out the road test, during the See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING there was a noise from the front identified as a noise coming from the passenger compartment fan. Move on to Step 1 1 FAN CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the climate control fan. In particular, check: that the fan and spiral is clean, if there are any foreign bodies, deposits of dust on the vanes and/or leaves remove them/blow through moving the fan from the engine support; that there are no breaks or cracks in the fan; there are no vibrations or noise at low speed (check the operation with the fan detached from the assembly but the electrical connection fitted). "The operation for determining vibrations should be carried out with great care wearing protective goggles to avoid fragments of the fan being expelled into the surrounding area" Move on to Step 2 1.Fan dirty 1.Clean the fan casing and all the ducts. 2.Presence of breaks or cracks in the fan. 2.Replace the fan. Op. 5040C30 AIR CONDITIONING FAN - R.R. 3. Electric motor noisy, fan not balanced or blades. 3. Replace the fan. Op. 5040C30 AIR CONDITIONING FAN - R.R. 2 AIR DUCT CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check for foreign bodies and damaged components inside the air ducts. Move on to Step 3 Presence of foreign bodies or damaged components inside the air ducts. Eliminate the obstructions from the dashboard ducts. 3 AIR VENT CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the vents are intact and that there are no foreign bodies that could give rise to noise. Move on to Step 4 Vents obstructed. Restore the operation of the vents. 4 POLLEN FILTER CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the pollen filter is not blocked and that the recirculation air intake is not blocked with foreign bodies or parts (e.g. wiring) that are not correctly fitted. Move on to Step 5 1. Filter obstructed. 1. Replace the filter element Op. 5010B09 PURIFYING (POLLEN) FILTER FILTER ELEMENT - REPLACE 2. Air intake blocked by foreign bodies. 2. Eliminate the obstructions and restore correct operation. 5 FAN INTAKE CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fan intake in the air intake chamber is not blocked by the presence of foreign bodies. End of diagnosis Presence of foreign bodies in the air intake chamber. Eliminate the obstructions and restore correct operation.

0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Lift the wper arms off the glass, turn on the panel and select one of the functions (e.g. intermittence) to see whether the noise persists. Move on to Step 1 The noise is no longer present. Replace the wiper blades and/or wiper arms. Op. 5050B28 WINDSCREEN WIPER BLADE/S - R+R Op. 5050B32 WINDSCREEN WIPER ARM/S - R+R 1 CHECK THE WIPER IS CORRECTLY FASTENED ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Turn off the function selected previously using the stalk command and turn off the panel. Then remove the wiper arms and panel to ensure the windscreen wiper is correctly fastened to the body. Op. 5050B32 Move on to Step 2 Incorrect fastening of the windscreen wiper. Restore the correct fastening of the windscreen wiper. 2 CHECK THE WINDSCREEN WIPER LINKAGE ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Turn off the instrument panel and check the linkage movement is correct, in particular: ensure the linkage does not interfere with the body or is hindered by foreign bodies present in the wiper housing. check that the windscreen wiper unit has been correctly assembled. End of diagnosis 1. The linkages interfere with the body. 1. Restore the linkages to correct working order. 2. Foreign bodies present in the windscreen wiper housing. 2. Remove the foreign bodies from the windscreen wiper housing. 3. Incorrect assembly of the windscreen wiper. 3. Replace the windscreen wiper unit Op. 5050B38 WINDSCREEN WIPER ASSEMBLY - R+R OR REPAIR

With the vehicle moving, particularly over rough ground or during acceleration or braking, noise can be heard from the dashboard area. 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Road test the vehicle to check the type of noise See Test 70B ROAD TEST FOR NOISE RECOGNITION Move directly to the relevant step. 1. Squeaking noise cannot be located. 1. Move on to Step 1. 2. Noise from one of the front doors. 2. Proceed as instructed in the See table S062 FRONT DOORS CREAKING 1 CHECK DASHBOARD/WINDSCREEN COUPLING ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the gap between the lower area of the windscreen and the dashboard is correct: the gap must be sufficiently large for a card to be inserted Move on to Step 2 Faulty dashboard fastening. Renew the felt pads behind the facia in the contact area with the windscreen. 2 CHECK OUTLET FASTENINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the air outlet fastening tabs on the dashboard. Move on to Step 3 1. Fault in central outlet fastening. 1. Renew the correct fastening Op. 5010C30 CENTRAL AIR VENT IN DASHBOARD - R.R. 2. Fault in side outlet fastening. 2. Renew the correct fastening Op. 5010C38 SIDE AIR VENT (ONE) LEFT OR RIGHT IN DASHBOARD - R.R. 3 CHECK GAUGE FASTENINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the correct fastening of the three gagues behind the steering wheel: in particular, check for the felt pads in the coupling area with the dashboard. Move on to Step 4 1. Faulty fastening of gauges behind the steering wheel. 1. Restore the correct fastening of the gauges. Replace the felt pads if necessary. See assembly Op. 5560B ANALOGUE CONTROL PANEL 2. Faulty fastening of check gauge behind the steering wheel. 2. Restore the correct fastening of the check gauge. Replace the felt pads if necessary. See assembly Op. 5560C OTHER INSTRUMENTS 4 CHECK STEERING COLUMN TRIM FASTENING ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the steering column trim is correctly fastened to the dashboard. In particular, check for: insulating material around the cables; felt pads in the mating area with the dashboard; free movement of the steering wheel height adjustment device; fastenings of the steering column cover sections. Move on to Step 5 Faulty fastening. Restore the correct fastening on the facia. Restore the felt pads if necessary Op. 7040A26 STEERING COLUMN TRIM - R+R 5 CHECK THE CENTRAL TRIM FASTENINGS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the central console trim is correctly fastened to the dashboard. In particular, check for: correct fastening of the central instrument module; insulating material around the cables; felt pads in the mating area with the dashboard; Move on to Step 6 1. Faulty central console fastening. 1. Renew the correct fastening. Restore the felt pads if necessary Op. 7040A60 UNDERDASHBOARD TRIM - R.R. 2. Faulty central instrument module fastening. 2. Renew the correct fastening Op. 5560C51 COMBINED ANALOGUE CONTROL PANEL - R+R OR REPLACE 6 CHECK THE CLIMATE CONTROL MODULE FASTENING ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the climate control unit is correctly fastened. Move on to Step 7 Faulty climate control unit fastening. Renew the correct fastening of the control unit Op. 5040D18 AIR CONDITIONING CONTROL UNIT - R.R. 7 CHECK THE GLOVE COMPARTMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the correct fastening of the dashboard glove compartment and its flap. In particular, check for the presence of the rubber pad used to secure the compartment to the dashboard. End of diagnosis 1. Faulty glove compartment fastening. 1. Restore the correct fastening of the glove compartment on the dashboard. Restore the felt pads if necessary Op. 7040A31 DASHBOARD COMPARTMENT ASSEMBLY - R.R. 2. Faulty flap fastening. 2. The climate control is working normally, but there are unpleasant smells in the passenger compartment. 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION First of all, check the following with the compressor ON: that the condensation drainage is not blocked; that condensation drains inside the passenger compartment; that the condensation drainage is not damaged; that the recirculation is not working; that there are no unpleasant smells coming from the outside by activating the recirculation Move on to Step 1 1. Condensation drainage blocked 1. Clean the condensation drainage 2. The condensation is draining directly into the passenger compartment. 2. Restore the correct operation of the condensation drainage. 3. Condensation drainage damaged. 3. Replace the condensation drainage. 4. Recirculation not working. 4. Continue as instructed in the See table L016 CLIMATE CONTROL RECIRCULATION NOT WORKING 5. Smells coming from the outside 5. Move on to Step 5 1 POLLEN FILTER CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the pollen filter. "The pollen filter should be replaced at least once a year". Move on to Step 2 Filter obstructed. Replace the filter element Op. 5010B09 PURIFYING (POLLEN) FILTER FILTER ELEMENT - REPLACE 2 AIR INLET DUCTS CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the air inlet ducts: they should not be obstructed with dirt or unpleasant smelling substances. Move on to Step 3 Ducts blocked. Wash the ducts. 3 EVAPORATOR CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION With the engine started and the climate control system off (compressor OFF button), place the temperature knob in the max heat position and activate the fan. Check that the bad smell disappears. Move on to Step 6 The smells persist. Move on to Step 4 4 RADIANT MASS CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fins of the radiant mass are not blocked with dirt or other substances. With the vehicle engine on, engine temperature warm or climate control system (temperature) knob set to max heat, check for fluid leaks inside the vehicle from the plastic tank or the radiant mass case. End of diagnosis 1. Radiant mass dirty or blocked. 1. Clean the radiant mass. 2. Fluid leak from the radiant mass. 2. Replace the radiant mass. 5 AIR INTAKE CHAMBER CLEANLINESS CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that there are no foreign bodies inside the air intake chamber. Check, in particular, that the seal between the air intake chamber and the engine compartment is perfect. End of diagnosis 1. Air intake chamber dirty. 1. Clean the air intake chamber. 2. Seal not perfect. 2. Restore the correct operation of the seal. 6 EVAPORATOR REPLACEMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Replacement of the evaporator (check whether it is possible to clean it) The use of Aircomatic equipment amd Wynn''s Airco-clean is recommended for disinfecting the mould on the evaporator and the directions should be followed. End of diagnosis Evaporator covered in mould Ask the customer whether it is the first time that the problem occurs, in which case the evaporator should be cleaned; If the customer complains for the 2nd time more than 6 months later, continue to clean the evaporator, if it is less than 6 months replace the evaporator Op. 5040C64 A/C EVAPORATOR - R+R

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0087 (Pressure at pipe) This error is detected if the pressure measured is too low. If necessary, replace the faulty components 4.Pipes obstructed or damaged 4.Renew the pipes. Step 5 5 Low supply pressure check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Constrict the return pipe, downstream of the valve, and carry out the test again with the pipe constricted checking that the The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0110 (Air flow meter temperature signal) This error is detected if the junction unit inlet voltage (Pin 53) is greater than 4.95 V (positive short circuit) (detail "Beyond the upper limit" or less than 0.05 V (short circuit to earth or break in the circuit) (detail "Below the lower limit"). In this case the junction unit replacement value is 40 °C. 1 SUPERCHARGING TEMPERATURE SENSOR CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the supercharging temperature sensor is working properly, following the instructions in the See Test 1064BD SUPERCHARGING TEMPERATURE CHECK End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0168 (Limit for high fuel temperature) This error is detected if there is a mechanical problem with the engine or if the system is overheating as a result of overloading The quantity of fuel injected is reduced as a result. 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the diagnostic equipment and select the Bosch EDC 16C39 electronic control unit, checking that none of the following errors are present: P0180 - Fuel temperature sensor P1612 - Fuel filter heating relay control Move on to Step 2 1. Error P0180 present 1. Proceed as instructed in the See Test 1060EA DIESEL FUEL TEMPERATURE CHECK 2. Error P1612 present 2. Proceed as instructed in the See Test 5505AC CHECK DIESEL PREHEATING RELAY 2 ENGINE COOLING SYSTEM CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the fuel cooling system is working properly Check the engine cooling system is working properly. Check that there are no engine oil leaks and that the engine oil level is correct Op. 0010T11 ENGINE OIL - CHECK LEVEL AND TOP UP, IF NECESSARY If all these conditions are followed, the malfunction is caused by poor use of the engine End of diagnosis 1. Malfunction of the fuel cooling system 1. Restore the correct operation of the system 2. Malfunction of the engine cooling system 2. Restore the correct operation of the system 3. Engine oil leaks 3. Continue as instructed in the See table X12 ENGINE OIL LEAKS 4. Engine oil level beyond permitted limits 4. Restore the correct engine oil level Op. 0010T11 ENGINE OIL - CHECK LEVEL AND TOP UP, IF NECESSARY

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0180 (Fuel temperature sensor) This error detects if the voltage at the junction unit inlet (Pin 11) is more than 4.96 V (positive short circuit) (detail "short circuit to +Vbatt") or if it less than 0.23 V (short circuit to earth or break in the circuit) (detail "short circuit to earth or open circuit) for at least 0.3 secs. In this case the control unit takes 50 °C as the replacement value. 1 FUEL TEMPERATURE SENSOR CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fuel temperature sensor is working properly, following the instructions in the See Test 1060EA DIESEL FUEL TEMPERATURE CHECK End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0190 (Fuel high pressure sensor) This error is detected if the voltage entering the junction unit (Pin 43) is more than 4.75 V (detail "short circuit to Vbatt") or if it is less than 0.25 V (detail "short circuit to earth or open circuit"). 1 FUEL HIGH PRESSURE SENSOR CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fuel high pressure sensor is working properly, following the instructions in the See Test 1060GH DIESEL FUEL PRESSURE CHECK End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0120 (Accelerator pedal sensor 1). This error is detected if, with fault code P0641 not recognized, the junction unit input voltage (Pin 9) is more than 4.67 V (positive short circuit) or less than 0.15 V (short circuit to earth or break in the circuit). As a result, the accelerator pedal does not work. 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the diagnostic equipment and select the Bosch EDC 16C39 electronic control unit, checking that none of the following errors are present: P0651 - Sensor power supply 2 Move on to Step 1 Error P0651 present Proceed as instructed in the See Test 1060GN CHECK ENGINE CONTROL UNIT CONNECTIONS 1 ACCELERATOR PEDAL CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the accelerator pedal is working properly See Test 1068AC ACCELERATOR PEDAL CHECKS End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0191 (Fuel pressure signal) This error is detected if there is interference with the signal for the sensor at Pin 43 of the electronic control module. 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the diagnostic equipment and select the Bosch EDC 16C39 electronic control unit, checking that none of the following errors are present: P0641 - Sensor power supply 1 P0651 - Sensor power supply 2 Move on to Step 1 1. Error P0641 present 1. Proceed as instructed in the See Test 1060GM CHECK ENGINE CONTROL UNIT CONNECTIONS 2. Error P0651 present 2. Proceed as instructed in the See Test 1060GN CHECK ENGINE CONTROL UNIT CONNECTIONS 1 ACCELERATOR PEDAL CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the accelerator pedal is working properly, carrying out the See Test 1068AC ACCELERATOR PEDAL CHECKS End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0220 (Accelerator pedal sensor 2). The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0230 (Fuel pump relay control) with detail "short circuit to +Vbatt" This error is detected if there is a positive short circuit or break in the circuit connected to Pin 28 of the junction unit for at least 0.3 secs. 1 Fuel pump check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the operation of the fuel pump relay by carrying out See Test 1040AB SUBMERGED FUEL PUMP CHECK End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0234 (Supercharging pressure). This error is detected if the supercharging pressure is too high or too low. As a result, the exhaust gas recirculation valve is switched off and the supercharging pressure can longer be controlled. 0 Preliminary checks ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the engine oil level is correct Op. 0010T11 ENGINE OIL - CHECK LEVEL AND TOP UP, IF NECESSARY Check that the air intake/vacuum circuit is working properly by carrying out the See Test 1048OA AIR INTAKE/VACUUM CIRCUIT CHECK Check the condition of the fuel supply circuit and make sure that it is working properly carrying out the See Test 1040OA FUEL SUPPLY CIRCUIT CHECK Check the operation of the low pressure supply circuit by carrying out the See Test 1060OB CHECK ON SUPPLY LOW PRESSURE FUEL CIRCUIT Move on to Step 1 Oil level incorrect Restore the correct engine oil level Op. 0010T11 ENGINE OIL - CHECK LEVEL AND TOP UP, IF NECESSARY 1 Ambient parameters check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Select the following control unit at the diagnostic equipment: EDC16C39 Diesel electronic injection control unit. Check the value of the following parameters: Supercharging pressure Objective Supercharging pressure Measured Overboost valve closure See Test 1060GF SUPERCHARGING PRESSURE CHECK End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0235 (Supercharging pressure sensor), with detail "short circuit to +Vbatt or open circuit" This error is detected if there is a positive short circuit or break in the circuit connected to Pin 7 of the junction unit. In addition, if there is a short circuit to the positive, the supercharging pressure can no longer be controlled. 1 Supercharging solenoid valve check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the supercharging pressure solenoid valve is working by carrying out the See Test 1064BB CHECK ON OPERATION OF SUPERCHARGING PRESSURE SOLENOID VALVE (PIERBURG) End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0235 (Supercharging pressure sensor), with detail "short circuit to earth" This error is detected if there is a short circuit to earth in the circuit connected to Pin 7 of the junction unit. As a result the maximum power is reduced and the exhaust gas recirculation valve is switched off. In addition the supercharging pressure can no longer be controlled 0 Preliminary checks ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check, in the junction unit under the dashboard, that fuse F35 has not blown (it is the second from the right in the top row) See B002 JUNCTION UNIT UNDER DASHBOARD Move on to Step 1 The fuse has blown Proceed as instructed in the See Test 1064BE CHECK TURBO VALVE PROTECTION FUSE 1 Supercharging solenoid valve check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the supercharging pressure solenoid valve is working by carrying out the See Test 1064BB CHECK ON OPERATION OF SUPERCHARGING PRESSURE SOLENOID VALVE (PIERBURG) End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0335 (Engine rpm sensor), with detail "signal not valid" This error is detected if the change in position of the crankshaft is not within the acceptable range of values or cannot be learnt. As a result, the engine is switched off. 0 Preliminary checks ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Select the following system on the diagnostic equipment: Diesel EDC16C39 electronic injection system. Delete the errors present and press the START/STOP button. Wait for the engine management control unit to switch off (min. 20 secs.). The main relay is switched off. If the engine is very hot, the fans remain on after the ignition is switched off. In this case, the control unit switches off automatically 10 secs after the fans are switched off. Proceed as instructed in the See Test 1060GL CHECK OPERATION OF MAIN ENGINE CONTROL UNIT RELAY

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0340 (Timing sensor), with detail "general electrical fault" This error is detected if the engine is running and the camshaft signal is not recognized. 1 Check on operation of timing sensor ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check correct operation of the timing sensor by carrying out the See Test 5510CG CHECK TIMING SENSOR OPERATION End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0340 (Timing sensor), with detail "signal plausibility" This error is detected if the engine is running and the control unit cannot synchronize the camshaft signal. 1 Engine speed check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the engine speed is correct by carrying out the See Test 1060GI ENGINE SPEED CHECK Move on to Step 2 2 Check on correct engine timing ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the engine timing is correct Op. 0510A20 TIMING GEAR WITH BELT DRIVE - CHECK - CARRY OUT OPERATION WITH CAM COVER(S) REMOVED AND TAPPETS ADJUSTED AND CRANKSHAFT PULLEY DETACHED (IF NECESSARY) Move on to Step 3 Timing not correct Restore the correct engine timing Op. 1032B10 TOOTHED TIMING BELT - R + R FOR TIMING ADJUSTMENT OR REPLACEMENT 3 Timing sensor check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check correct operation of the timing sensor by carrying out the See Test 5510CG CHECK TIMING SENSOR OPERATION End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0685 (main relay), with detail "actuator slipping" This error is detected if the main relay switches off too late or does not switch off at all. The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P010F (air mass/flow meter inconsistency). This error is detected if the engine speed is below 50 rpm and the difference between the supercharging pressure and the barometric pressure sensor is more than 0.15 bar for at least 10 sec. As a result, the control unit carries out the calculations with a replacement value of 1.013 bar, the maximum power is reduced and the supercharging pressure can no longer be controlled. 1 PRESSURE CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the value of the atmospheric pressure, by carrying out the See Test 1060GD ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE CHECK Check the value of the supercharging pressure, by carrying out the See Test 1060GF SUPERCHARGING PRESSURE CHECK End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0111 (flow meter air temp. signal). This error is detected if there is interference with the signal for the sensor at Pin 37 of the electronic control module (detail "general electrical fault") or if there is a short circuit to positive (detail "beyond the upper limit") or to earth (detail "below the lower limit") in the circuit connected to Pin 37 of the control unit. In the case of short circuits, the control unit takes 25 °C as the replacement value. 1 FLOW METER OPERATION CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the flow meter is working properly by carrying out the See Test 1060GS DEBIMETER OPERATION CHECK End of diagnosis

The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0778 (fuel pressure regulator (high pressure pump outlet or pipe). CHECK TO BE PERFORMED RESOLUTION IF THE CHECK IS NOT OK 1 Remove the pump from the fuel tank and draw the fuel from the bottom of the tank. Fill a 100 ml glass cylinder with 1 ml graduations with this fuel to the 90 ml level. Add 10 ml of water to reach the 100 ml level and close the cover. Shake the cylinder vigorously for 10-15 seconds, then remove the cover paying attention: some of the alcohol vapours naturally present in the fuel will escape. Close the cover and shake the cylinder again for 10-15 seconds. Leave the cylinder to rest on a horizontal surface for about 5 minutes to allow the liquids to separate 2 Check that there is not a liquid layer in the lower part of the cylinder (colloid suspension of water and alcohol) that exceeds a level of 10 ml Remove the fuel from the tank and clean the actual tank 3 Draw off 0.5 litres of fuel from the bottom of the tank. Fill a glass container with this fuel. Leave the container to rest on a horizontal surface for about 5 minutes to allow the sedimentation of the particles in suspension. Check that there are no white or light brown crystals (sand) or irregular black particles (rubber) Remove the fuel from the tank and clean the actual tank

The fuel system is highly sensitive. The work must be carried out with the greatest cleanliness and care. Any air in the system could damage the high pressure fuel pump. The vehicle must therefore never be driven with the fuel tank empty. CHECK TO BE PERFORMED RESOLUTION IF THE CHECK IS NOT OK 1 Check that the tank contains the correct type of fuel Remove the content and wash the tank 2 The fuel reserve must be greater than 5 litres. Put back a fuel quantity of at least 5 litres 3 Check for leaks in the fuel circuit. Install fitting 1.870.752.000 between the turbocharging sensor and the intake chamber. Connect the pressure transducer to the tool. Position the diagnostic equipment in the passenger compartment and make the connections. Select "pressure gauge" on the diagnostic equipment and prepare for the acquisition of data in "intake pressure" mode with a 2000 mmHg full scale deflection and select a time of 10 seconds. Road test the vehicle (observing the speed limits in force) and perform the following test: - On a motorway route, allow the vehicle to reach 2500 rpm in 4th gear. - Initiate graphic acquistion by pressing start on the diagnostic equipment and 2 seconds later fully depress the accelerator pedal until the engine speed is 3500 rpm. - Once this speed is reached completely release the accelerator pedal. - Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant section, with the exception of the initial peak, the reading should be 1900 -2080 mbar (1444 -1581 mmHg) corresponding to a supercharging value of 900 -1080 mbar. - On a motorway route with fast-moving traffic, let the vehicle reach 2500 rpm in 3rd gear. - Initiate graphic acquistion by pressing start on the diagnostic equipment and 2 seconds later fully depress the accelerator pedal until the engine speed is 3500 rpm. - Once this speed is reached completely release the accelerator pedal. - Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant section, with the exception of the initial peak, the reading should be 1900 -2080 mbar (1444 -1581 mmHg) corresponding to a supercharging value of 900 -1080 mbar.

- Carry out a road test on traffic free roads in safe conditions following the highway code. - Before proceeding with the test, check the inflation pressure of the two vehicles, restoring the values to the correct ones if they are found to be incorrect. - Also check the conditions of the wheel rims making sure they are not distorted or broken, replacing them if any faults are found. - Carry out the test on an uneven road surface, at a speed of 40 km/h to check the capacity of the suspension to absorb the stresses produced by small imperfections (suspension damping) with the consesquent acoustic repercussions inside the passenger compartment. - Check the capacity of the suspension to absorb the stresses produced by large imperfections and the consequent acoustic repercussions inside the passenger compartment, carry out the road test at a speed of 40 km/h over a route that has a series of pot-holes. - Check the rapid damping of any pitching produced by the irregularities in the road surface, carrying out the test at a speed of 50 km/h on a straight road with suitably spaced humps and holes. - This type of test should always be used for comparison with a new vehicle or reference vehicle of the same trim level and engine type, available in the workshop at the time of the test in question. - At the end of the test in question, assess/rate the driving comfort of the vehicle in accordance with the enclosed table. Do not check the air conditioning system in the immediate vicinity of the walls (distance of approximately 2 m) in order to ensure sufficient circulation of the air by the condenser. Set the required passenger compartment temperature to COLD (turn anticlockwise to stop). Set the fan to 4th speed. Switch on the air conditioning (LED on snowflake symbol on). Take the reading from the high pressure gauge and ensure it is greater than 13 bars Move on to Step 4 2 Check the cooling fan is on. Move on to Step 4 Move on to Step 3 3 Turn the ignition key to the ON position. With the engine off, perform active diagnosis on the cooling fan and ensure it is successful Restore the electrical connections between the fan and engine control unit See E5020 ENGINE COOLING If necessary, replace the fan Op. 1088E10 RADIATOR COOLING FAN - R + R Before draining the air conditioning system, check the coolant circuit to ensure there are no leaks Op. 5040A14 AIR CONDITIONING REFRIGERANT CIRCUIT - CHECK FOR LEAKS AND ELIMINATE IF NECESSARY BY TIGHTENING CONNECTORS Check the connection to the expansion valve in particular. Disconnect the electrical connection for the linear sensor. See K120 LINEAR SENSOR FOR FANS Check that Pin 1 is earthed and Pin 2 is at +5V. Connect a linear potentiometer (end of scale 1 KOhm, previously positioned at around 500 ohm between the centre pin andone of the side ones) to the pins of the linear sensor electrical connector. Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Using a multimeter, check that the voltage between pins 1 and 3 is around 2.5V. Switch on the engine and switch on the air conditioning using the special switch located on the climate control system control unit. The climate control system should come on normally in these circumstances. Alter the potentiometer resistance until the voltage reading on the multimeter between pins 1 and 3 is about 0 V. The air conditioning system should switch off in these conditions because the engine management node receives low circuit pressure information. Alter the potentiometer resistance until the voltage reading on the multimeter between pins 1 and 3 is about 4.6V. The air conditioning system should switch off in these conditions because the engine management node receives high circuit pressure information.

Disconnect the electrical connector for the passenger compartment air fan maximum speed relay See J041 Connect a multimeter in ohmmeter mode between the following pins and measure: Between pins 1 and 4 a resistance of between 0.352 and 0.288 Ohm. Between pins 1 and 2 a resistance of between 2.232 and 1.488 Ohm. Between pins 1 and 2 a resistance of between 0.946 and 3 Ohm.

Using an Examiner set to the Voltmeter mode, select a 20 Volt full scale deflection and 5 seconds, connect the black probe to the vehicle earth and the red probe on pin 3 of the mist sensor output signal, turn the key on and press the START button. The signal shown should be a set of PWM impulses with a frequency of 100 Hz and a Duty Cycle that varies between 10 and 90% as indicated in the table below. The first 100 sensor output readings should not be considered (about 1 sec). 1. earth 2. +15 3. not connected 4. signal output PWM% Duty Cycle = T1 / T2 where: T1= duration of impulse T2 = 1/f = 1/100 Hz = Duratation of transmission T2 = 10msec ± 7% PWM of 20% at 70% This is the normal sensor operating range. Within this range, the sensor supplies a PWM signal proportional to the amount of condensation present on the windscreen. PWM = 10% Indicates an internal sensor fault. This fault is defined as follows: the sensor self-diagnosis detected an internal electrical problem. PWM = 80% This condition indicates a sensor limit condition. This is defined as follows: The sensor optics are saturated due to too much direct sunlight. The signal is transmitted as long as the limit condition described above persists. PWM = 90% This condition indicates a sensor limit condition or failure. It is defined as one of the following: The sensor optics are saturated due to too much reflected energy. This may be due to a very high level of condensation or an object between the windscreen surface and the sensor. The internal sensor temperature reached and exceeded 70°C. The internal processor is disabled to avoid damage. A fault signal is transmitted as long as the excess temperature persists. PWM = 0 % and 100% These two conditions will never be transmitted by the sensor. Specific hardware faults may be interpreted by the receiving input stage as PWM signals or 0% or 100% due to the static nature of the signal (microcomputer that does not process or conditions of dc to +12V or GND or open circuits). Messages transmitted by PWM 100% Sensor " off " or fault in communication or d.c. to +12 V 90% Sensor saturated or locked in excess temperature 80% Sensor faulty or subject to direct sunlight 70% Condensation intensity Max to moderate 60% Condensation intensity moderate to slight 50% Condensation intensity light to identifiable 40% Condensation intensity slightly visible 30% Condensation intensity not visible to the human eye 20% Windscreen clean - No condensation 10% Internal sensor fault. 0% Sensor " off " or fault in communication or d.c. to GND

STEP CHECK TO BE PERFORMED RESOLUTION IF THE CHECK IS NOT OK 1 Check the protected power supply from the instrument panel. If the power supply is not OK, replace the instrument panel. If OK, replace the auxiliary instruments. 2 Check serial line 1. If there is no serial line signal at the panel output, replace the instrument panel. Take the vehicle on the road under safe conditions and respecting the highway code Turn on the CRUISE CONTROL system and set the ON/OFF switch on the CRUISE CONTROL stalk to ON Check the Cruise Control warning light comes on. Drive the vehicle at 50 or 70 km/h in 4th gear (according to the maximum speed limit on the road). Turn the wheel on the CRUISE CONTROL stalk towards SET + and release it immediately to store the speed reached. Remove your foot from the accelerator and check the vehicle maintains the set speed. Turn the wheel on the CRUISE CONTROL stalk toward the SET+ position and maintain the position to increase the speed to 70 or 90 km/h (according to maximum speed limit on the road). do not operate the accelerator. Release the control wheel and maintain the set speed for a few seconds. Press the BRAKE pedal and release immediately, then wait for the vehicle speed to drop to 50 or 70 km/h do not operate the clutch. Press and release the RESUME key on the end of the stalk and check that the vehicle returns to the last stored speed value (70 or 90 km/h, according to the level set previously). do not operate the accelerator. Press the CLUTCH pedal and release immediately, then wait for the vehicle speed to drop to 50 or 70 km/h do not operate the brake Press and release the RECALL key on the end of the CRUISE CONTROL stalk and check that the vehicle returns to the last stored speed value (70 or 90 km/h, according to the level set previously). do not operate the accelerator. The key remote control is supplied by a CR2032 lithium battery (3 V, 220 mAh), remote control operation is ensured between 2.6 and 3.6 V with a maximum current of 15 mA. At least 9000 activations of 1 s duration and 3000 activations of 5 s duration are guaranteed over a period of two years. The battery voltage is monitored to check the charge level: the threshold is set at 2.6±0.06 V. If the remote control receiver detects that the battery is flat, it is still possible to carry out a total of 100 operations. Operating frequency: 433.92 MHz. CHECK TO BE PERFORMED RESOLUTION IF THE CHECK IS NOT OK 1 Take out the key battery and connect the diagnostic instrument in Voltmeter mode to the key terminals with the correct polarity. Check that the voltage exceeds 2.2 Volts. Replace the battery Note that after replacing the battery, the remote control variable code must be re-synchronised: this operation is carried out by pressing the remote control key twice. Note that if the remote control has been activated more than 255 times, variable code synchrony between the sending unit and the receiver will be lost (the receiver will no longer be able to identify a variable code message correctly). Synchrony should therefore be restored by pressing the remote control unit key twice.

Check the operation of the satellite navigation system Check that the map disc is consistent with the vehicle model. In NAV mode, check that the number of satellites in the last line on the right is at least 3 indicating that the satellite reception is correct. If the reading for the number of satellites is less than 3 then the reception is not good enough to locate the vehicle. It is probably a question of insufficient cover. In this case try and move the vehicle to an area where there is good reception or compare the reception with other cars located in the same place. The satellite reception test should be carried out in an open area. In this case, without a comparison it is impossible to say whether or not the navigator is defective. If, on the other hand, the comparison reveals even worse reception, check the connection of the satellite aerial, the electrical continuity, the correct power supply and, if necessary, test with different equipment that is definitely working properly. For the road test: Exit to NAV mode Check that the arrow moves consistently with the vehicle speed, otherwise check the presence of the milometer signal. Check that the arrow changes direction in line with the vehicle. If the arrow does not change direction this means that the gyroscope inside the map reader is broken and the Connect should be replaced. Enter a destination and activate the calculation of the route. Wait for the first instruction and the route on the display and check that it is correct. Irregular instructions: before or after junctions, arrow out of position, they may be due to CD maps that are not up to date: a missing instruction stems from the fact that a road is not on the map because it has not been processed in digital form or the road network has been changed compared with the one on the map. The navigator calculates the position of the vehicle both by means of the satellite signal and using the wheel rpm and the internal gyroscope bush signal. Problems of accuracy may arise when: The odometer speed signal and reversing signal are not received correctly Occasions when the navigation system should be initialised: The vehicle is being transported with the battery disconnected and travelling in a tunnel (the navigator loses the references). Immediately after having changed the tyres (since the wheel rpm/distance conversion factor is not accurate). When replacing the Nit. To initialize the navigator it is necessary to drive about 100 km in optimum satellite reception conditions. If all the tests have not highlighted defects then the problem lies in the Connect which should be replaced.

Apply a solution of soapy water to the entire perimeter of the glass. From inside the passenger compartment, blow through with compressed air along the entire perimeter, moving the trims to the side and the top, if necessary. Visually inspect for any bubbles of air on the outer surface: this makes it possible to locate any areas where the sealant is not sufficient or damaged. If there is a lack of sealant on the vertical pillars, the pillar trim can be moved and rubber type sealant can be injected from the inside. If there is a lack of sealant on the top section, the roof lining can be moved and rubber type sealant can be injected from the inside. If there is a lack of sealant on the bottom section, the trim at the base of the (front) windscreen or the rear parcel shelf (for the rearscreen) can be moved and rubber type sealant can be injected from the inside. If there is insufficient sealant in widespread areas, the overall seal of the window cannot be guaranteed and therefore it has to be removed and the windscreen or the rearscreen must be completely resealed. Op. 7035A18 WINDSCREEN GLASS - R.R INCLUDING CLEANING HOUSING

ATTENTION All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid personal injury.The engine compartment contains many moving parts, components at high temperatures and live wires. Follow the warnings given below very carefully when working in the engine compartment: turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down, do not smoke, do not use naked flames and ensure a fire extinguisher is available.The use of special tools is required for certain procedures. The use of these tools is vital for working in safety.Follow the current workshop safety regulations. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific procedures to be followed to prevent dangerous situations from arising.For the use of chemical products, follow the safety instructions on the card from the supplier to the consumer.The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000 V and above which could be very hazardous to people especially if they are suffering from a heart condition. Therefore take great care when working on these systems or in the vicinity of their components. WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key where there is no longer a traditional ignition key having been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G." (Transmitter for Entry and go) combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vheicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated in the TEG takes place in entirely the same as with the traditional remote control incorporated in the key fob.The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a conventional key.Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid damage to components.To release parts that are sticking, tap gently using an aluminium or lead mallet if iron materials are involved; use a wooden or resin mallet for light alloy parts.When dismantling, check that components that should be marked have the appropriate references.When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent seizing during the initial operating period. When refitting it is vital to respect the adjustment nut tightening torques.Each time they are refitted, replace gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safetly plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated screws and all parts that have deteriorated.Use adhesive paper or clean cloths to suitably protect those parts of the engine which, if they remain uncovered after dismantling, will allow dust or foreign bodies to enter.Only genuine spare parts should be used to replace units or components that have been removed. this is the only way of ensuring the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components. When the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the same condition (released or locked) as previously. Whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected during workshop operations, leave the TEG inserted when disconnecting the battery: the steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn.

During this operation keep the climate control system switched off to prevent the fan from coming on for reasons unconnected to the heating of the coolant. - If the level in the reservoir drops considerably during this stage, restore the engine idle speed and open the filler cap very carefully and top up to the MAX level; then close the cap completely and finish the bleeding of the air from the engine cooling system. - Stop the engine for around 1 minute and wait for any air bubbles from the thermostat to rise towards the engine coolant reservoir. - Start the engine again and carry out another cycle of accelerations and fan engagements. - Stop the engine and wait for a sufficient drop in the engine coolant temperature. - After the above operations, check the fluid level in the reservoir and top up to the MAX notch on the reservoir if necessary. - At the end of the above operations, make sure that the amount of fluid introduced into the system is at least equal to the amount collected during the draining stage.
