DESCRIPTION The car is equipped with numerous light sources for optimal lighting of interior instruments and controls. Some of these are lit with the ignition ON (INT), others with the side lights on, others are dimmable in accordance with a rheostat-controlled adjustment strategy managed by the Body Computer. The Body Computer manages the lighting - with the side lights on - of: - cigar lighter and rear current socket; - controls on the front courtesy light - radio display (aftermarket version only) See E3510 RADIO - radio phone preparation See E3580 PREPARATION FOR CELLULAR TELEPHONE The Body Computer manages (directly and via the door control units) the dimmed lighting of: - instrument panel and display; - auxiliary instrument - switches in the doors; - climate control system controls. All the other controls are lit up when the ignition is on (INT), i.e. with the TEG inserted. A brightness sensor for the automatic adjustment (day/night) of the brightness of the instrument panel is built-in; it has the task of measuring the ambient light conditions and sending this information (daytime or nightime) to the Body Computer which, on comparing this information with the state of the side lights, selects the appropriate lighting configuration for the vehicle interior (daytime or nightime mode). DESCRIPTION The vehicle is equipped with a horn system consisting of two horns with different tones: one high tone and one low tone: the two horns come on simultaneously. The horns are operated by pressing the sides of the steering wheel cover (around the Air Bag). The horn circuit is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by a relay located in the engine compartment junction unit. For safety reasons, the horns can be operated at any time even with the TEG switched off.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The system for the horns receives a power supply via the horn relay T3 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 from the line directly from the battery via fuse F10 in junction unit B1. The relay coil is energized by an earth signal produced by the closing of one of the switches on the steering wheel, connected via the wiring through the clock spring D47. The relay thereby supplies the horns P05.

DESCRIPTION The windscreen wash/wipe system is activated by the lever located on the right of the steering wheel, with the following functions: there are five possible positions for the lever, turning it upwards, corresponding to: - windscreen wiper off (stationary); - intermittent/automatic operation; - continuous slow operation; - continuous fast operation; - "antipanic" temporary fast operation (unstable position, turning the lever downwards). In the intermittent/automatic operation position three different positions can be selected by turning the ring nut: - on the "LOW" version the different intermittent speeds are switched on (from the slowest to the fastest; - on the "HIGH" version with the rain sensor: the different sensor settings are switched on: the activation of the rain sensor involves a windscreen wiper arm stroke as feedback to confirm that it has been switched on. The frequency of the windscreen wiper strokes is automatically adjusted depending on the amount of water on the windscreen detected by the sensor: the frequency varies continuously from nil (no stroke - windscreen dry) to wiping at the second continuous speed (heavy rain). The windscreen washer function can be activated by pulling the lever toward the steering wheel: this activates the windscreen washer pump: keeping the lever pulled also switched on the windscreen wiper in accordance with a specific control logic: the windscreen wiper is activated at the first speed: when the windscreen washer control is no longer present, an additional stroke is carried out. The screen washer fluid reservoir has a sensor that signals a decrease in the level by means of a special warning light in the instrument panel. The control of the functions described above is carried out by an electronic device inside the steering column switch unit which produces the intermittent function and controls the operation of the windscreen wiper motor and the windscreen washer electric pump. The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by the ignition-operated exclusion relay (INT/A) located in the junction unit under the dashboard. The windscreen wiper and the windscreen washer can be activated with the TEG inserted and after starting (INT/A). The correct operation of the rain sensor is controlled by the check function. If the rain sensor is not working properly, the windscreen wiper will operate intermittently whilst the instrument panel display will show the sensor failure.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The electronic device inside the steering column switch unit H5 and the controls on the right lever receive a power supply at pin 11 of connector A from the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) of relay T12 protected by fuse F43, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B2. Pin 7 of connector A and 9 of connector C of H5 are earthed. According to the function selected, stalk unit H5 (connector A) sends the following control signals to the wiper motor N15: - from pin 8 for fast operation; - from pin 9 for slow and/or intermittent operation, - pin 6, on the other hand, receives the earth signal coming from the motor end of travel cam which stops operation. The windscreen wiper motor N15 is then earthed. The steering column switch unit H5 windscreen washer switch, once activated, sends two signals from pins 10 and 12 of connector A which operate the windscreen washer pump N22 which turns sending the detergent liquid to the windscreen wiper. The rain sensor housed in the mirror P65 receives a supply from the INT line protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit B2 and sends the automatic operating signal to pin 2 of connector A of H5 via the A-BUS serial line of the Body Computer M1 pin 7 of connector D and pin 25 of connector B. The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 to manage the failure signal if there are problems with the rain sensor. The screen washer fluid level sensor k27 sends an earth signal to the instrument panel E50 - pin 12 of connector D - which lights up the warning light directly.

DESCRIPTION The rear wiper control is activated by turning the three-position wheel anticlockwise: - stable central position, equivalent to OFF; - 2 unstable positions: rear wiper activation and rear washer activation. The rear wiper is controlled by the stalk intermittently with an interval of 5 seconds between the end of one stroke and the beginning of the next. The motor is activated throughout the duration of the command and until the brush is reparked. With the windscreen wipers working, if reverse gear is engaged, the rearscreen wiper is automatically activated: this function is managed by the Body Computer, which receives information from the reversing switch See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION Pushing the right steering column switch unit lever activates the rear washing. Keeping the lever pushed for more than 0.5 secs automatically activates the rearscreen wiper at the continuous speed. The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by the ignition-operated exclusion relay (INT/A) located in the junction unit under the dashboard. The windscreen wiper and the windscreen washer can be activated with the TEG inserted and after starting (INT/A).

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The electronic device inside the steering column switch unit H5 and the controls on the right lever receive a power supply at pin 11 of connector A from the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) of relay T12 protected by fuse F43, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B2. Pin 7 of connector A and 9 of connector C of H5 are earthed. The electronic device inside the steering column switch unit H5, which controls the rear wiper receive a power supply at pin 12 of connector C from the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) of relay T12 protected by fuse F52, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B2. Steering wheel stalk unit H5 sends a command to rear wiper motor N16 from pin 1 of connector B while pin 2 receives an earth signal from the motor end stop cam, which stops operation. Pin 3 of connector A of H5 receives the reverse engaged signal for automatic rear wiper operation. The steering column switch unit H5 windscreen washer switch, once activated, sends two signals from pins 10 and 12 of connector A which operate the windscreen washer pump N22 which turns sending the washer fluid to the windscreen wiper.

DESCRIPTION The headlamp washer cleans the headlamp lenses as the windscreen is being cleaned. The headlamp washer function is managed by the Body Computer which automatically activates the headlamp washer, with the dipped headlamps on, when the windscreen washers are activated through the lever on the right of the steering wheel. The headlamp washer consists of a pump that sends detergent to two nozzles located in the bumpers which spray a powerful jet onto the headlamps. A timer activates the headlamp washer pump by means of a series of pulses lasting about half a second. The headlamp washer circuit is protected by a fuse and governed by a special relay located in the engine compartment junction unit.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The relay T17 in the engine compartment junction unit B1 receives a power supply from the line for fuse F9, from the engine compartment junction unit B1, whilst the energizing takes place through the ignition-operated line (INT/A) from fuse F31 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2. The relay operates the headlamp washer pump N25 directly when an earth signal arrives from the Body Computer M1; this signal - from pin 14 of connector A - is sent on the basis of the positive windscreen washer request signal coming from the steering column switch unit H5 - pin 5 of connector A and in the presence of the dipped headlamps on enablement (pin 2 of connector I and pin 28 of connector G of M1). See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS

DESCRIPTION In the case of poor visibility it is possible to activate the demisting of the rearscreen, the exterior rear view mirrors and the lower part of the windscreen. The heating resistances for these components absorb a considerable amount of energy and are therefore controlled and, possibly, deactivated after they have been working for a certain length of time: the demisting is subject to a delay timer, managed by the Body Computer, according to the following logic: - TEG inserted, starting excluded (INT/A); - engagement signal coming from the special button in the climate control system control panel. Under these circumstances the resistances remain supplied for a maximum of 20 minutes, then the supply is cut off. The supply is cut off in the following conditions: - TEG extracted (key-off); - disengagement signal from the button; - battery voltage below 8.5 V; - after the first 15 minutes of operation if the engine speed is below 960 rpm. With the defrosting on the warning light in the climate control system controls also comes on. The activation timer (20 minutes) is set again each time the button is operated. The climate control system control unit logic also intervenes with the "MAX-DEF" command in accordance with the logic described previously. The "MAX-DEF" function lasts for 3 minutes starting from when the engine temperature exceeds a certain limit. the deactivation of the MAX-DEF control only causes the switching off of the heated rear windscreen if the command to switch it on came from the MAX-DEF button; if, on the other hand, the command was given via the heated rear windscreen button, it remains on) The rearscreen defrosting circuit is controlled by the heated rear windscreen relay and protected by a specific fuse, located in the junction unit under the dashboard. This circuit is controlled by the logic described above directly by the Body Computer. The defrosting circuit for the door mirrors, on the other hand, is protected by another fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard and is controlled by the door control units, in accordance with the logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN. The windscreen defrosting circuit is operated by a special relay located in the engine compartment junction unit and protected by a specific fuse also in that junction unit.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The heated rear windscreen relay T11, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, controls the engagement of the heated rear windscreen P55 defrosting resistances via the line protected by fuse F40 of junction unit B2. Similarly, the engagement of the defrosting resistances for the windscreen P56 are operated via the line protected by fuse F41 of junction unit B2 and relay T19 and fuse F20 located in the engine compartment junction unit B1. The coil for relay T11 receives an ignition-operated power supply (INT/A) and is energized by an earth signal coming from the Body Computer M1 - pin 6 of connector F; this signal is sent on the basis of the previously illustrated control logic and in the presence of the heated rear windscreen engagement command or through the MAX-DEF function coming via the CAN from the climate control system control unit M70. The engagement of the defrosting resistances for the door mirrors P60 and P61 is controlled by the control units for the driver''s door M66 and passenger door M67 connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1. Control units M66 and M67 receive a supply - at pin 11 of connector D - from the line protected by fuse F32 of underfacia control unit B2 . On the basis of the complex control logic illustrated previously, the engagement command for the defrosting is sent via the CAN to the two door control units as well which control the resistances located in mirrors P60 and P61 from pins 7 and 9 of connector E of M66 and M67.

DESCRIPTION In the case of poor visibility it is possible to activate the demisting of the rearscreen and the exterior rear view mirrors. The heating resistances for these components absorb a considerable amount of energy and are therefore controlled and, possibly, deactivated after they have been working for a certain length of time: the demisting is subject to a delay timer, managed by the Body Computer, according to the following logic: - TEG inserted, starting excluded (INT/A); - engagement signal coming from the special button in the climate control system control panel. Under these circumstances the resistances remain supplied for a maximum of 20 minutes, then the supply is cut off. The supply is cut off in the following conditions: - TEG extracted (key-off); - disengagement signal from the button; - battery voltage below 8.5 V; - after the first 15 minutes of operation if the engine speed is below 960 rpm. With the defrosting on the warning light in the climate control system controls also comes on. The activation timer (20 minutes) is set again each time the button is operated. The climate control system control unit logic also intervenes with the "MAX-DEF" command in accordance with the logic described previously. The "MAX-DEF" function lasts for 3 minutes starting from when the engine temperature exceeds a certain limit. the deactivation of the MAX-DEF control only causes the switching off of the heated rear windscreen if the command to switch it on came from the MAX-DEF button; if, on the other hand, the command was given via the heated rear windscreen button, it remains on) The rearscreen defrosting circuit is controlled by the heated rear windscreen relay and protected by a specific fuse, located in the junction unit under the dashboard. This circuit is controlled by the logic described above directly by the Body Computer. The defrosting circuit for the door mirrors, on the other hand, is protected by another fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard and is controlled by the door control units, in accordance with the logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The heated rear windscreen relay T11, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, controls the engagement of the heated rear windscreen P55 defrosting resistances via the line protected by fuse F40 of junction unit B2. The coil for relay T11 receives an ignition-operated power supply (INT/A) and is energized by an earth signal coming from the Body Computer M1 - pin 6 of connector F; this signal is sent on the basis of the previously illustrated control logic and in the presence of the heated rear windscreen engagement command or through the MAX-DEF function coming via the CAN from the climate control system control unit M70. The engagement of the defrosting resistances for the door mirrors P60 and P61 is controlled by the control units for the driver''s door M66 and the passenger door M67. Control units M66 and M67 receive a supply - at pin 5 of connector C and 11 of connector A - from the line protected by fuse F41 of junction unit under the dashboard B2 .

DESCRIPTION The door mirrors can be electrically adjusted in two directions using a joystick control located in the door controls on the driver''s side: a selection cursor makes it possible to choose either the left or the right mirror. The button controls two electrical motors located in each of the two mirrors: one motor allows the rotation of the mirror on the horizontal axis, another on the vertical axis. The circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard and is operated by the door control unit in accordance with the control logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Control unit M66 is supplied at pin 11 of connector D - by a line protected by fuse F36 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 . The controls on the driver''s door H44 include the joystick and control switch for the exterior rear view mirrors: - selection of the right/left mirror: signal to pin 30 of connector A of M66, - vertical movement: signal to pin 28 of connector A of M66, - horizontal movement: signal to pin 29 of connector A of M66. On the basis of the commands received, the control unit M66 controls the motor for the mirrors P60 from pin 4 of connector E (joint) and for pins 3 and 5 (horizontal and vertical movement respectively). Similarly, the same commands are sent to the passenger side mirror P61 from pins 10, 26 and 27 of connector B of M66.

DESCRIPTION The door mirrors can be electrically adjusted in two directions using a joystick control located in the door controls on the driver''s side: a selection cursor makes it possible to choose either the left or the right mirror. The button controls two electrical motors located in each of the two mirrors: one motor allows the rotation of the mirror on the horizontal axis, another on the vertical axis. Another button controls the folding back of the mirrors if required (for example when trying to get through a narrow space). On the HIGH version, in addition to moving the door mirrors manually, it is possible to memorize and later on recall 3 positions defined in relation to the position of the driver''s seat; the passenger side rear view mirror is also positioned automatically when reverse gear is engaged. This entire complex logic is managed by the driver''s seat control unit which converses with the Body Computer via the CAN See E3076 ELECTRICALLY-ADJUSTABLE SEATS The interior rear view mirror is electrochrome type: i.e. it contains an electronic device which controls the automatic anti-glare function. The automatic antiglare function is disabled when reverse is engaged. The circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard and is operated by the door control units in accordance with the control logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN. The interior rear view mirror power supply circuit is protected by a fuse in the under-dashboard control unit.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The motors for the exterior rear view mirrors in P60 and P61 are operated by the driver''s door control unit M66 and the passenger door control unit M67, connected to one another via the CAN line and to the Body Computer M1 and to the driver''s seat movement and memory control unit H66. See E3076 ELECTRICALLY-ADJUSTABLE SEATS The two mirrors contain a potentiometer for each motor which detects the position and sends a feedback signal to the control unit to pins 10 and 11 of connector E of M66 and M67. (pins 15 and 17 of connector E provide a power supply and earth for the potentiometers). Control units M66 and M67 receive a supply - at pin 11 of connector D - from the line protected by fuse F32 of underfacia control unit B2 . The controls on the driver''s door H44 include the joystick and control switch for the exterior rear view mirrors: - selection of the right/left mirror: signal to pin 30 of connector A of M66, - vertical movement: signal to pin 28 of connector A of M66, - horizontal movement: signal to pin 29 of connector A of M66, - mirror folding: signal to pin 20 of connector B of M66. On the basis of the requests set whilst driving or on the basis of values memorized, the control units M66 and M67 control the motors for mirrors P60 and P61 from pin 4 of connector E (joint) and pins 3 and 5 (horizontal and vertical movement respectively). The folding motors are controlled from pins 1 and 8 of connector E of M66 and M67. Electrochrome mirror P65 supplies an ignition-controlled power supply (INT) - from pin 23 of connector D - from a line protected by fuse F32 of under-dashboard control unit B2. The switch for the reversing lights I20 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the fuse line F35 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2. When reverse is engaged, the switch closes to send a control signal to mirror P65 through control unit B2 - from pin 8 of connector D.

DESCRIPTION The simultaneous operation of the four door locks takes place via: - TEG the remote control; - the locking/unlocking button in the centre console. The TEG remote has 3 buttons which allow the operation of the central locking system: a button for unlocking the doors, one for locking the vehicle and one for releasing the boot See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING The door unlocking/locking management strategy is carried out by the door control unit which controls the effective state of the locks through the signals arriving from the switches in the actual locks and the emergency key pawl (driver''s door only) in this way the "locking" command is only carried out with all the doors properly shut and the locks unlocked; conversely, the "unlocking" command is only carried out with the locks locked. The locks have an additional motor that carries out the dead lock function which allows the interior door opening handles to be mechanically disconnected so that it is no longer possible to open the door from the inside (for example, after having broken the glass in a theft attempt); the dead lock function also inhibits the operation of the door locking/unlocking buttons in the dashboard. The dead lock function is switched on at the time the doors are locked or by pressing the remote control twice. An LED next to the two above mentioned controls makes the following signals: - locking of the locks: the LED lights up for 3 seconds. If some of the doors or the boot are not properly shut at the time when the locks are locked, the LED flashes at 3 Hz for 3 seconds; - dead lock activation: the LED flashes twice for 0.5 seconds; - unlocking the locks: the LED goes out. The instrument panel acquires the door status signal via the CAN and lights up the "doors open" warning light and, at the same time, the information is shown on the display; in addition, if one of the doors or the boot or the bonnet is open and the speed of the vehicle exceeds around 4 km/h, an acoustic warning is also emitted. It is possible, using the special setup in the instrument panel, to select whether to unlock all the doors or only the driver''s front door, whilst all the other doors and the boot remain locked. It is possible to enable/disable the locking of the doors above a certain speed threshold (20 km/h) using the special setup in the instrument panel: in this case the Body Computer implements the locking of the doors when this threshold is exceeded. When the speed returns below this level, the doors and the boot remain locked; later on, when one of the doors is opened, the function is re-enabled and, if the threshold is exceeded, the doors are locked once again. The boot unlocking operating mode can be selected still using the special setup in the instrument panel: - assisted boot unlocking: the tailgate is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes; - independent boot unlocking: the boot is locked when the doors are locked, whilst it can be unlocked independently of the unlocking of the doors. See E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING - DESCRIPTION The doors are automatically unlocked if the inertia switch is operated: the instrument panel receives a signal from the switch, lights up the appropriate warning light and notifies the Body Computer via the CAN. The central locking circuit is protected by a specific fuse located in the junction unit under the dashboard.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The locking/unlocking function for the doors is operated by the front doors control unit M66 connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1. Control unit M66 is supplied at pin 11 of connector D - by a line protected by fuse F36 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 . Pin 19 connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 are earthed. The control unit M66 receives the following inputs: - the "locking" signals from the four knobs, at pin 23 of connector B of and 7 of connector C of M66; - the locking/unlocking signals from the emergency key pawl, at pins 24 and 25 of connector B of M66; - the negative signal from the locking/unlocking button, located in the controls on the tunnel H35, at pin 34 of connector A of M66. According to the control logic illustrated, the control unit M66 controls the geared motors for the four door locks and the fuel flap: the joint power supply for the motors is sent from pins 6 and 5 of connector D; the locking/unlocking motors (B/S) are operated from pins 4 and 2 of connector D; the dead lock motors (DL) for locks N50 and N51 are operated from pins 3 and 1 of connector D. N55, N56. The signalling LED E40 is lit up by a signal from pin 8 of connector C of M66, whilst a reference earth is sent from pin 6. The activation of the inertia switch I50 is indicated at pin 17 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 : this signal, as described previously, causes the opening of the doors.

DESCRIPTION The simultaneous operation of the four door locks takes place via: - TEG the remote control; - the locking/unlocking button in the centre console. The TEG remote has 3 buttons which allow the operation of the central locking system: a button for unlocking the doors, one for locking the vehicle and one for releasing the boot See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING The door unlocking/locking management strategy is carried out by the two door opening controls units and the boot control unit (for the rear doors) which control the effective state of the locks through the signals arriving from the switches in the actual locks and the emergency key pawl (driver''s door only) in this way the "locking" command is only carried out with all the doors properly shut and the locks unlocked; conversely, the "unlocking" command is only carried out with the locks locked. The locks have an additional motor that carries out the dead lock function which allows the interior door opening handles to be mechanically disconnected so that it is no longer possible to open the door from the inside (for example, after having broken the glass in a theft attempt); the dead lock function also inhibits the operation of the door locking/unlocking buttons in the dashboard. The dead lock function is switched on at the time the doors are locked or by pressing the remote control twice. An LED next to the two above mentioned controls makes the following signals: - locking of the locks: the LED lights up for 3 seconds. If some of the doors or the boot are not properly shut at the time when the locks are locked, the LED flashes at 3 Hz for 3 seconds; - dead lock activation: the LED flashes twice for 0.5 seconds; - unlocking the locks: the LED goes out. The instrument panel acquires the door status signal via the CAN and lights up the "doors open" warning light and, at the same time, the information is shown on the display; in addition, if one of the doors or the boot or the bonnet is open and the speed of the vehicle exceeds around 4 km/h, an acoustic warning is also emitted. It is possible, using the special setup in the instrument panel, to select whether to unlock all the doors or only the driver''s front door, whilst all the other doors and the boot remain locked. It is possible to enable/disable the locking of the doors above a certain speed threshold (20 km/h) using the special setup in the instrument panel: in this case the Body Computer implements the locking of the doors when this threshold is exceeded. When the speed returns below this level, the doors and the boot remain locked; later on, when one of the doors is opened, the function is re-enabled and, if the threshold is exceeded, the doors are locked once again. The boot unlocking operating mode can be selected still using the special setup in the instrument panel: - assisted boot unlocking: the tailgate is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes; - independent boot unlocking: the boot is locked when the doors are locked, whilst it can be unlocked independently of the unlocking of the doors. See E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING - DESCRIPTION The doors are automatically unlocked if the inertia switch is operated: the instrument panel receives a signal from the switch, lights up the appropriate warning light and notifies the Body Computer via the CAN. The central locking circuit is protected by two specific fuses - one for the front doors and one for the rear doors - located in the junction unit under the dashboard.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The door locking/unlocking function is controlled by the control units for the driver''s door M66, passenger side M67 and luggage compartment M63 all connected via the CAN line to one another and to the Body Computer M1. The control units M66 and M67 receive a power supply at pin 11 of connector D from the line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2, the luggage compartment junction unit M63 at pin B8 of connector A from the line protected by fuse F36 of B2. Pin 19 connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 and of M67 are earthed. Pin C8 of connector A of M63 is also earthed. Control units M66 and M67 receive the following input: - the "locking" signals from the knobs at pin 23 of connector B of M66 and M67; (the knobs for the rear doors send the signal to the passenger side control unit M67; - the locking/unlocking signals from the emergency key pawl, at pins 24 and 25 of connector B of M66; - the negative signal from the locking/unlocking button, located in the controls on the tunnel H35, at pin 34 of connector A of M66. According to the control logic illustrated, the control units M66 and M67 control the geared motors for the front door locks: the joint power supply for the motors is sent from pin 6 of connector D; the locking/unlocking motors (B/S) are operated from pin 4 of connector D; the dead lock motors (DL) for locks N50 and N51 are operated from pin 3 of connector D. Similarly the control unit M63 receives control signals from pins 10, 11 and 26 of connector B of M67 and controls the geared motors for the rear door locks: the joint power supply for the motors is sent from pin A7 of connector A and A2 of connector B; the locking/unlocking motors (B/S) are operated from pin C7 of connector A and C2 of connector B; the dead lock motors (DL) for locks N55 and N56 are operated from pin C6 of connector A and C4 of connector B. The signalling LED E40 is lit up by a signal from pin 8 of connector C of M66, whilst a reference earth is sent from pin 6. The activation of the inertia switch I50 is indicated at pin 17 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 : this signal, as described previously, causes the opening of the doors.

DESCRIPTION The boot opening geared motor is operated by: - the special button in the courtesy light; - the remote control (TEG). Operation through the remote control takes place in two ways. - indepedently of the doors: there is a special button on the remote control that allows the boot only to be "unlocked": the boot is released and lifts up slightly. The operation is signalled by the direction indicators flashing twice; when it is closed again the boot returns to the state prior to opening. - together and at the same time as the unlocking of the doors: the tailgate is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes: for the control logic. See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING One of the two modes described above can be selected using a special setup in the instrument panel. The boot opening function via the button in the courtesy light is disabled (the boot does not open) if the speed of the vehicle is above 10 km/h. The fuel flap is managed directly by the driver''s door node and is therefore connected to the locked/unlocked status of the driver''s door. The boot opening circuit is protected by a specific fuse, located in the junction unit under the dashboard.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The "boot open" signal is sent by the switch - located in the courtesy light G10 - to pin 35 of connector E of the Body Computer M1. The boot unlocking function, inside the Body Computer M1 pin 1 of connector F also has a dedicated earth connection: pin 20 of connector F. (HIGH version) or from pins 4 and 6 of connector D of M66 LOW version); See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING Control unit M66 is supplied at pin 11 of connector D - by a line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 . The control units in the door control the operation of the driver''s and passenger side electric window motors which are operated both manually and automatically depending on the version. Automatic operation takes place as follows: - if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed; - f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted); - pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in; - if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock). DESCRIPTION The electric windows for the front doors are operated through the switches on the driver''s door (both windows) and the passenger side (passenger side only). The control units in the door control the operation of the driver''s and passenger side electric window motors which are operated both manually and automatically depending on the version. Automatic operation takes place as follows: - if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed; - f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted); - pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in; - if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock). Each control unit in the door also manages the anti-crush safety function: it acquires information concerning the possible presence of an obstacle whilst the glass is closing (upwards movement): a resistive sensor is inserted in an outer casing fitted to the upper seal which is compressed if there is an obstacle preventing the window from closing properly: under these circumstances the control unit immediately interrupts the travel of the glass and reverses it until it is in the bottom end of travel position. The correct operation of the anti-crush sensor is controlled by the control unit check function: in the case of a failure this information is sent via the CAN to the instrument panel to show the information on the display. In addition, if a fault is detected, the control unit inhibits the automatic raising operation only allowing it in steps of 500 ms each time the button is pressed. The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button. The circuit is controlled by the services relay and protected by two fuses located in the junction unit under the dashboard: there is a power supply both with the TEG inserted (ON) and not inserted (OFF); during the starting stage this relay is temporarily deactivated whilst with the TEG not inserted (OFF) the Body Computer keeps the relay activated for 3 minutes but deactivates it 30 seconds after one of the doors is opened. The driver''s door control unit acquires both the driver''s front door and passenger side front door commands; it manages the movement of the driver''s window directly and sends the relevant movement commands for the passenger side window via the CAN to the passenger door control unit which manages the passenger side window directly.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The services relay T13, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, supplies pin 14 of connector F, the two control units for the driver''s door M66 and the passenger door M67, pin 8 of connector D, through the control logic described above and controlled by the Body Computer M1, via two lines protected by fuses F47 and F48. Pins 19 of connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 and M67 are earthed. Control units M66 and M67 are connected via the CAN line to one another and to the Body Computer M1. Unit H44 contains the driver and passenger side window controls:: dedicated analogue signals are sent to pins 31 and 32 of connector A of M66 (pin 33 supplies a reference earth).. Similarly, the control at the passenger front door H50 sends a special analogue signal to the control unit M67 pin 32 (pin 33 provides the reference earth). Control unit M66 operates the motor N60 (driver''s side) directly - pins 9 and 10 of connector D - and via control unit M67 - pins 9 and 19 of connector D - motor N61 (passenger side). Pins 2 and 5 of connector C of M66 and M67 also receive signals from the anti-crush safety sensors K22 and K23 . The two control units are connected to the instrument panel E50 via the CAN line to manage the signal if there is a failure in the anti-crush safety sensors.

DESCRIPTION The electric windows for the front doors are operated through the switches on the driver''s door (both windows) and the passenger side (passenger side only). The control units in the door control the operation of the driver''s and passenger side electric window motors which are operated both manually and automatically depending on the version. Automatic operation takes place as follows: - if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed; - f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted); - pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in; - if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock). Each control unit in the door also manages the anti-crush safety function: it acquires information concerning the possible presence of an obstacle whilst the glass is closing (upwards movement): a resistive sensor is inserted in an outer casing fitted to the upper seal which is compressed if there is an obstacle preventing the window from closing properly: under these circumstances the control unit immediately interrupts the travel of the glass and reverses it until it is in the bottom end of travel position. The correct operation of the anti-crush sensor is controlled by the control unit check function: in the case of a failure this information is sent via the CAN to the instrument panel to show the information on the display. In addition, if a fault is detected, the control unit inhibits the automatic raising operation only allowing it in steps of 500 ms each time the button is pressed. The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button. The circuit is controlled by the services relay and protected by two fuses located in the junction unit under the dashboard: there is a power supply both with the TEG inserted (ON) and not inserted (OFF); during the starting stage this relay is temporarily deactivated whilst with the TEG not inserted (OFF) the Body Computer keeps the relay activated for 3 minutes but deactivates it 30 seconds after one of the doors is opened. The driver''s door control unit acquires both the driver''s front door and passenger side front door commands; it manages the movement of the driver''s window directly and sends the relevant movement commands for the passenger side window via the CAN to the passenger door control unit which manages the passenger side window directly.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The services relay T13, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, supplies pin 14 of connector F, the two control units for the driver''s door M66 and the passenger door M67, pin 8 of connector D, through the control logic described above and controlled by the Body Computer M1, via two lines protected by fuses F47 and F48. Pins 19 of connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 and M67 are earthed. Control units M66 and M67 are connected via the CAN line to one another and to the Body Computer M1. Unit H44 contains the driver and passenger side window controls:: dedicated analogue signals are sent to pins 31 and 32 of connector A of M66 (pin 33 supplies a reference earth).. Similarly, the control at the passenger front door H50 sends a special analogue signal to the control unit M67 pin 32 (pin 33 provides the reference earth). Control unit M66 operates the motor N60 (driver''s side) directly - pins 9 and 10 of connector D - and via control unit M67 - pins 9 and 19 of connector D - motor N61 (passenger side). Pins 2 and 5 of connector C of M66 and M67 also receive signals from the anti-crush safety sensors K22 and K23 . The two control units are connected to the instrument panel E50 via the CAN line to manage the signal if there is a failure in the anti-crush safety sensors.

DESCRIPTION The electric windows in the rear doors are activated using the switches in the actual doors and the driver''s front door. The luggage compartment junction unit checks the operation of the rear electric window motors directly. The commands from the driver''s front door are transmitted via the CAN from the control unit in the door. The electric window motors are operated either manually or automatically, depending on the trim level. Automatic operation takes place as follows: - if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed; - f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted); - pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in; - if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock). The luggage compartment junction unit also manages the anti-crush safety function: it acquires information concerning the possible presence of an obstacle whilst the glass is closing (upwards movement): a resistive sensor is inserted in an outer casing fitted to the upper seal which is compressed if there is an obstacle preventing the window from closing properly: under these circumstances the control unit immediately interrupts the travel of the window and reverses it to the lower end of travel position. The correct operation of the anti-crush sensor is controlled by the control unit check function: in the case of a failure this information is sent via the CAN to the instrument panel to show the information on the display. In addition, if a fault is detected, the control unit inhibits the automatic raising operation only allowing it in steps of 500ms each time the button is pressed. The circuit is operated according to the luggage compartment junction unit control logic with a power supply protected by two special fuses operated by the underdashboard junction unit services relay: there is a power supply both with the TEG inserted (ON) and not inserted (OFF); during the starting stage this relay is temporarily deactivated whilst with the TEG not inserted (OFF) the Body Computer keeps the relay activated for 3 minutes but deactivates it 30 seconds after one of the doors is opened. The driver''s front door control unit also manages the locking of the rear controls (protection) when the special LOCK button is pressed: the locking status is indicated by an LED in the back of the actual button lighting up and the rear control buttons are not lit up. The electric windows cannot be operated using any of the buttons when the lock function is activated. The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The services relay T13, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, supplies the luggage compartment junction unit (which manages the rear electric windows) M63 pin A8 of connector A and pin B8 of connector B, with the logic described above and controlled by the Body Computer M1 pin 14 of connector F, via two lines protected by fuses F33 and F34 of B2. Pins B1 and C8 of connector A and pin A1 of connector B of M63 are earthed. The junction unit is connected via the CAN line to the driver''s front door control unit M66. The unit H44 also incorporates the controls for the rear windows and the LOCK button: special analogue signals are sent to pins 27 of connector B and 1 and 3 of connector C of M66 (pin 33 of connector A provides the reference earth). With the LOCK button pressed the control unit M66 relays the signal for switching on the relevant LED in H44 (from pin 7 of connector C); the control unit M66 then transmits these signals to control unit M63 via the CAN. Similarly, the controls at the rear doors H53 and H54 send dedicated analogue signals to the control unit M63 to pins B5 of connectors A and B. The control unit M63 operates the motors N65 (left) - from pins A1 and C1 of connector A and N66 (right) - from pins A8 and C8 of connector B. The signals for the anti-crush sensors K19 and K24 reach pins A5 and B3 of connector A of M63 and pins A4 and A6 of connector B of M63. The control units M63 is also connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1 and to the instrument panel E50 to manage the signal if there is a failure in the anti-crush safety sensors.

DESCRIPTION The sun-roof provides a means of extra passenger compartment ventilation and ensures swift air exchange when necessary for improved passenger comfort. The system is operated by a knob near the front courtesy light. The roof operating strategy is controlled by a special control unit that receives signals from the control knob and the roof operating motor. When the control knob is turned in the direction shown by the arrow, the roof slides open: a choice of 5 opening positions is available; return the knob to the central position to close the roof. The sun-roof is equipped with a blind underneath that slides manually but is pushed along by the roof when it opens. The blind emerges slightly when the roof is closed to provide access to the manoeuvring handle. When the control handle is turned the opposite way to the direction shown by the arrow, the roof swivels up at the rear: a choice of 3 opening positions is available; return the knob to the central position to close the roof. Press the knob to interrupt all movement (inhibition position). The electronic roof control circuit also includes an antipinch function: whilst the roof is being closed, themovement is interrupted and reversed by about 10 cm if an obstacle is dtected by a Hall effect sensor located on the motor. This function can be excluded for safety reasons by pressing the knob as described above. The sun roof is also automatically opened through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button. The sun roof is also automatically closed - if left open - through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button. The circuit is controlled by the services relay and protected by a specific fuse, both located in the junction unit under the dashboard: there is a power supply both with the TEG inserted (ON) and not inserted (OFF) during the starting stage this relay is temporarily deactivated whilst with the TEG not inserted (OFF) the Body Computer keeps the relay activated for 3 minutes but deactivates it 30 seconds after one of the doors is opened.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The services relay T13, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, supplies the sun roof control motor N35 - pin 7 - via the line protected by fuse F46 of B2 through the logic described above and controlled by the Body Computer M1. The roof moving enablement/go ahead signal reaches pin 9 of N35 in accordance with the logic described above coming from pin 10 of connector D of the Body Computer M1. Pin 8 of N35 receives the speedometer signal from pin 28 of connector B of the Body Computer M1. Pin 10 of N35 is earthed, whilst pin 1 of N35 sends a power supply to switch H60 which relays the various control signals corresponding to the various positions of the knob to pins 2, 3, 4 and 5 of N35.

DESCRIPTION There is a standard type current socket on the tunnel console next to the handbrake, which can be used for the cigar lighter or for connecting instruments or equipment operating on 12 V. There is a second current socket the same as the first one in the end section of the tunnel console towards the rear seats. In the STATION WAGON version there is also a third current socket similar to the other two, located on the left-hand side of the luggage compartment. The cigar lighter heater coil can be placed in the front socket of the console; simply press the knob to operate it: after a few seconds it will come out automatically, ready for use. The two sockets on the console have a ring nut that lights up when the side lights are on. See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS The sockets are equipped with a thermal protection device: this protection cuts off the power supply if devices that absorb a lot of energy are connected. The circuit for the two current sockets in the console is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by the ignition-operated exclusion relay located in the junction unit under the dashboard. These sockets are ignition-operated (INT/A), to prevent the battery from being run down. The circuit for the luggage compartment current socket is also controlled by an ignition-operated (INT/A) exclusion relay and protected by a specific fuse, located in the luggage compartment fuse box.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Current socket/ cigar lighter P50 and the one at the back on the tunnel P51 receive a power supply from the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) of relay T12 and are protected by fuses F44 and F52 respectively, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B2. In the STATION WAGON version the rear current socket P52 power supply arrives via the relay T21 located in the fuse box in the boot B45; this is energized by the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) which arrives directly from the steering lock node M89; fuse F55, also located in B45, protects the P52 power supply circuit. Unlike the other two, the rear current socket does not have a ring nut that lights up when the side lights are switched on.

DESCRIPTION The front seats are available, on request, with a special heating system (comprising two heating elements located in the cushion and the backrest): this allows the seat to be heated to overcome the discomfort of cold passenger compartments in very harsh climates, e.g. when the car is left in the open for long periods in winter. The heating device located in each seat consists of two resistors activated by a controls located on the outside of each seat: there is a ring nut through which the function is switched on/off and the heating is adjusted to 3 different settings (0 = seat heating switched off). Once a certain temperature has been reached the heating stops automatically thanks to a thermal contact inside the actual device. A special LED in the actual switches indicates that the resistances are switched on. The seat heating can only be activated with the ignition on (INT/A). The seat heating circuit is controlled by a special relay and protected by two specific fuses located in the fuse box in the boot.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The seat heating power supply arrives via the relay T21 located in the fuse box in the boot B45; this is energized by the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) which arrives directly from the steering lock node M89; fuses F57 and F67, located in B45, protect the supply circuit for the two seats: the power supply for the two heaters O40 and O41 takes place via the control units M170 and M110 which receive commands from the switches I65 and I66. The switches are lit up with the ignition on (INT) by the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2.

DESCRIPTION The vehicle can be fitted with electrically adjustable front seats. A multifunction control on each seat includes: - adjustment of the backrest angle; - lengthwise adjustment of the seat; - front and rear height adjustment of the seat (rocker). The system also makes it possible to memorize and recall three different positions for the driver''s seat (and the door mirrors): after the position of the seat and the door mirrors has been adjusted, pressing one of the buttons ("1", "2" or "3") for a few seconds memorizes the position; this can only take place with the TEG inserted (ON). To recall a previously memorized position briefly press the relevant button. When a new seat position is memorized any previously memorized settings on this button are automatically cancelled Seat position memorization does not include heating start up See E3075 HEATED SEATS The seat is also equipped with a lumbar adjustment knob that makes it possible to improve comfort by altering the backrest support: this adjustment is always mechanical and not controlled by electric motors. The seat moving circuit is protected by two specific fuses located in the luggage compartment fuse box.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The driver''s seat H66 and passenger seat H67 control units control the entire system. The control knobs and buttons for the various functions are built into the control units themselves. The power supply to H66 and H67 - to pin 9 of connector A - passes through fuses F56 and F60, located in the luggage compartment fuse box B45 Pin 5 of connector A and 8 of connector B of H66 and H67 are earthed. Pins 5 and 6 of connector B of H66 and H67 are connected to the Body Computer M1 via the CAN. The two control units N66 and H67 control the various motors that move the seats in accordance with the logic described above: - adjustment of the backrest angle: motor N132 or N135 controlled; - lengthwise adjustment (sliding) of the seat: motor N127 or N130 controlled; - height adjustment of the cushion - front section: motor N125 or N128 controlled; - height adjustment of the cushion - rear section (rocker): motor N126 or N129 controlled;

DESCRIPTION The vehicle is fitted with two GAS DISCHARGE headlamps. The electronics in each of the two headlamps switches the gas discharge bulbs on and off at the times defined by the software and in accordance with international legislation. The system for each lamp comprises an igniter located at the base of the bulb and a ballast located in the lower part of the lamp. The left lamp is the master control unit whilst the right one carries out a slave role. The master acquires the command for the dipped headlamps, the vehicle speed and from the potentiometers located on the wheel axles. Depending on the inputs, the control unit controls the relevant adjustment motor, located in the headlamps, directly and tilts it as appropriate. For more details See descriptions 5540 EXTERIOR LIGHTING On versions with gas discharge headlamps, the light beam is adjusted automatically and there is no activation of the selector in the panel on the left side. The device is enabled only with the dipped beams on. The electronics for the two headlamps receive a supply from a fuse which protects other ignition-controlled power supplies.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Both electronic systems inside the headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right) are supplied - pin 9 - from the INT line of junction unit B2 protected by fuse F37. Pins 12 of the two control units are connected to one another by means of a special serial line, whilst the speedometer signal from the Body Computer M1 (pin 28 of connector B) reaches pin 10 of the junction unit located in headlamp F10. Pins 11 of the two headlamps are connected to the diagnostic K line See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR The Body Computer M1 controls the supply for the dipped headlamps sending an earth signal to relay T1 in the junction unit under the dashboard B2 from pin 8 of connector F of M1 which energizes relay T1: this supplies the dipped headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right). Each circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit B2 : F13 for the left headlamp and F12 for the right. The headlamp alignment function, managed by the connection F10B, is incorporated in the headlamp F10: the two sensors (potentiometers) that measure the geometry at the front K1 and at the rear K2 are connected; on the basis of these signals, the headlamp electronics automatically adjust the light beam by means of a special motor (the motor for the left headlamp is regulated directly, whilst the one for the right headlamp is adjusted via the serial line between F10 and F11).

DESCRIPTION The adjustment of the headlamp light beam according to the load is carried out by means of a special device (located inside the front light cluster) which tilts it appropriately, lowering the light beam if the vehicle is heavily laden and raising it if the load lessens. A special wheel, located in the controls to the left of the steering wheel, allows the adjustment of the headlamps in 4 vertical positions from 0 to 3: - position 0: one or two persons in the front seats, full fuel tank, fully equipped (vehicle in running order); - position 1: five persons; - position 2: five persons with full luggage compartment (about 50 kg); - position 3: driver and 300 kg load, all stowed in the luggage compartment (full load); The device is enabled only with the dipped beams on. The relay which controls the engagement of the dipped headlamps also supplies the adjustment motors inside the headlamps; this relay for switching the dipped headlamps on is managed by the Body Computer: the relay energizing is activated by TEG inserted (INT) enablement signals and by the steering column switch unit dipped headlamps control.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The dipped headlamps activation (earth) signal - and any AUTO function - is sent to pin 2 of connector I and to pin 28 of connector G of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5 See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS The Body Computer M1 controls the supply for the dipped headlamps sending an earth signal to relay T1 in the junction unit under the dashboard B2 from pin 8 of connector F of M1 which energizes relay T1: the latter supplies the dipped headlamps - pin 2 for the lamps F10 (left) and F11 (right); at the same time it provides the enablement for the adjustment motors - pin 6 for lamps F10 (left) and F11 (right); Each circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit B2 : F13 for the left headlamp and F12 for the right. The control for the headlamp adjustment, located in the unit to the left of the steering wheel H90, also receives the enablement supply - pin 5 of connector A, whilst a control signal produced by the adjustment potentiometer - pin 15 of connector B is sent; this control signal "passes through" the junction unit under the dashboard B and activates the adjustment motors built into the headlamps - pin 7 for the (left) lamps F10 and F11 (right).

DESCRIPTION The "Parking Assistance" system supplies the driver with information on distance when approaching obstacles (both behind and in front of the vehicle) thereby providing help with parking manoeuvres and identifying obstacles that are outside the field of vision. The information concerning the presence or distance of the obstacle is transmitted to the driver by means of acoustic and visual signals: - the frequency of the acoustic impulse warnings depends on the distance of the obstacle from the bumper. - the display in the instrument panel shows the areas around the vehicle which start flashing if the system detects that the vehicle is getting close to an obstacle. The system is activated if the following conditions are present simultaneously: - Key ON (TEG inserted) - reverse gear engaged or activation button - located on the front courtesy light - pressed (with the speed below 15 km/h). When the system is activated the buzzer warns of this condition and the LED is lit up. The system is deactivated: - by pressing the button again; - by disengaging reverse gear and when the vehicle speed is above 18 km/h. The LED goes out when the system is deactivated. The distance measurement only takes place when the system is activated, whilst only the control unit is operational in the inactive state. An electronic control unit activates and controls the operation of the sensors located in the front bumper and in the rear bumper, processes the signals received and operates the buzzers, one at the front and one at the back: the first is located on the cover under the dashboard on the driver''s side, the second is located in the luggage compartment at the base of the right rear pillar. The sensors use ultrasound technology and act as intelligent transmitters/receivers with triangulation technology: allowing improved detection in critical situations or in the presence of small obstacles. The impulses emitted are reflected by any obstacles; the transducer receives an echo which is converted into a digital signal and sent to the electronic control unit. The signalling of the distance of the obstacle is achieved through sound and visual signals: - the sound from the buzzer warns the driver that the vehicle is approaching an obstacle: the pause between the sounds is directly proportional to the distance from the obstacle, whilst a continuous sound indicates that the obstacle is less than 30 cm away; - the instrument panel display with the system activated shows the various areas around the vehicle, 7 front and 8 rear. The various areas are, in the various cases, either off, flashing or on constantly. For more details and information on the operation of the system, See descriptions 5580H PARKING OBSTACLE DETECTION DEVICE The control unit is equipped with an autodiagnostic function: when switched on the control unit carries out an initial test on the sensors which are then continuously subject to fault diagnosis during the operation of the system. A fault in only one sensor inhibits the operation of the entire system which is deactivated. Any faults/errors are signalled in the instrument panel by the relevant warning light coming on and the message in the display. The system is supplied by the circuit protected by a specific fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The parking sensor control unit M84 receives a supply at pin 1 of connector A from the ignition-controlled INT line protected by fuse F49 of junction unit B2; pin 8 of connector A is earthed. The control unit is connected, via pins 7 and 4 of connector A and the CAN, to all the other nodes in the same network, for example receiving the information that reverse gear is engaged. The commands for the display are sent to the instrument panel via the CAN. The signal from the activation/deactivation button, located in the courtesy light G10, reaches pin 4 of connector A. The positive signal that lights up the LED next to the button is sent from pin 13 of connector A. The front buzzer P44A is connected to pins 3 and 4 of connector B. The rear buzzer P44B is connected to pins 1 and 10 of connector A. The four front parking sensors K97 are connected to connector B of the control unit M84: pin 1 provides the reference earth, pin 2 the power supply, pins 5, 6, 7 and 8 are connected to sensors K97A, K97B, K97C and K97D, respectively. The four rear parking sensors K97 are connected to connector C of the control unit M84: pin 1 provides the reference earth, pin 6 the power supply, pins 5, 3, 2 and 4 are connected to sensors K97E, K97F, K97G and K97H, respectively.

DESCRIPTION The vehicle is equipped with a radio system comprising: - radio; - front speakers (woofers in the doors and tweeters in the dashboard); - rear speakers located in the doors - cables connecting the radio with the speakers; - aerial with support fitted at the rear of the roof with a coaxial connecting cable. A sophisticated Bose HIFI system with special HIFI speakers and an outside amplifier can also be fitted. On the version with the built in "CONNECT NAV +" radio-telephone-navigator the radio is incorporated in the unit. The aerial has three functions (radio/GSM/GPS) for the operation of the telephone and for the navigator. The radio is a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and with the other electronic units. The radio is equipped with an anti-theft system through the connection of the radio at the CAN with the Body Computer; it also manages the volume control linked to the vehicle speed: the volume increases and decreases in relation to the speed of the vehicle: this information reaches the radio node via the CAN. Some versions are equipped with a series of buttons on the steering wheel: these make it possible to replicate some of the commands which are acquired in the same way by the actual radio. It is also possible to fit a multi-polar cable connecting the radio to a CD player located in the boot, on the right hand side. See descriptions 5580P CONNECT PANEL

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Radio P20 is supplied directly (7 of connector A) from the battery via the line of fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 . The radio P20 receives an ignition-operated (INT) power supply (pin 4 of connector A) via the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 . Pin 8 of connector A is earthed. Pins 1 and 3 of connector A receive the CAN line by which the radio P20 is connected to the Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes. The radio P20 is connected, via the CAN, to the radio controls on the steering wheel, via the clock spring D47. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The following cables with signals for the speakers leave connector B of P20: - pins 5 and 6 to the left front speakers P35 and P45; - pins 3 and 4 to the right front speakers P36 and P46; - pins 7 and 8 to the left rear speakers P30 and P47; - pins 1 and 2 to the right rear speakers P31 and P48; The aerial P25 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable. A connection lead runs from connector E of P20 to CD player P75:. this cable, is divided into two sections: one under the dashboard and one under the passenger compartment lining (coupling D96).

DESCRIPTION The vehicle can be fitted, on request, with a simple preparation, (opt. 082) which includes a simple power supply for the radio not fitted on the vehicle, but installed in the aftermarket in accordance with the following ISO standard pin out: (connector A of P20): - pin 1: n.c. (mute) - pin 2: n.c. - pin 3: n.c. - pin 5: Bose amplifier presence signal - pin 6: +lights control lighting - pin 7: ignition-operated power supply +15 - pin 8: earth The radio installed in the AFTERMARKET is therefore not a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and with the other electronic units. The vehicle is equipped with preparation comprising: - front speakers (woofers in the doors and tweeters in the dashboard); - rear speakers located in the doors - cables connecting the radio with the speakers; - aerial with support fitted at the rear of the roof with a coaxial connecting cable. A sophisticated Bose HIFI system with special HIFI speakers and an outside amplifier can also be fitted.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Radio P20 is supplied directly (4 of connector A) from the battery via the line of fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 . The radio P20 receives an ignition-operated (INT) power supply (pin 7 of connector A) via the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 . Pin 8 of connector A is earthed. Pin 6 of connector A of P20 receives the power supply for the dimmer lighting, coming from pin 18 of connector H of M1. See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS The following cables with signals for the speakers leave connector B of P20: - pins 5 and 6 to the left front speakers P35 and P45; - pins 3 and 4 to the right front speakers P36 and P46; - pins 7 and 8 to the left rear speakers P30 and P47; - pins 1 and 2 to the right rear speakers P31 and P48; The aerial P25 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable.

DESCRIPTION A sophisticated Bose HIFI system with special HIFI speakers and an outside amplifier is available on request. The system has been developed ad hoc for the vehicle: the acoustic properties of the passenger compartment have been carefully studied so that the amplifier and the speakers are ideally suited to the vehicle: optimum listening is available in any part of the passenger compartment. Unlike the system fitted as standard, the Bose system offers: - special speakers at front and rear, which are midwoofers with separate tweeters; - subwoofer rear speaker located under the rear parcel shelf; - centerfill speaker located in the centre of the dashboard under the centre air vent; - high power amplifier located under the rear parcel shelf in the boot. The system is completed by a microphone, located in the centre courtesy light, which detects background noise in the passenger compartment: the signal is sent for amplification allowing the optimum adjustment and equalizing of the output levels. The other components (radio, aerial, etc.) are the same as the standard system. For more details See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Radio P20 is supplied directly (pin 4 and 2 of connector A) from the battery via the line of fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 . Pin 8 of connector A is earthed. Pins 1 and 3 of connector A receive the CAN line by which the radio P20 is connected to the Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes. The radio P20 is connected, via the CAN, to the radio controls on the steering wheel, via the clock spring D47. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The amplifier P70 receives a direct supply from the battery - at pin 31 - via the line for fuse F54 of the fuse box in the boot B45; pin 2 of amplifier P70 is earthed. Pin 6 of P70 is connected via a line to radio P20 - pin 6 of connector C - which supplies a positive signal to enable the amplifier to be switched on. The cables with signals for the speakers leave from connector B of P20; these signals are sent to the BOSE amplifier P70 which controls the actual speakers: - pins 5 and 6 of P20 to pins 7 and 19 of P70 and to the left front speakers P35 and P45 - pins 31 and 32 of P70 ; - pins 3 and 4 of P20 to pins 8 and 20 of P70 and to the right front speakers P36 and P46 - pins 26 and 27 of P70; - pins 7 and 8 of P20 to pins 9 and 21 of P70 and to the left rear speakers P30 and P47 - pins 4 and 16 of P70; - pins 1 and 2 of P20 to pins 10 and 22 of P70 and to the right rear speakers P31 and P48 - pins 5 and 37 of P70; The other signals leaving the BOSE amplifier P70 control the specific speakers: - centerfill P32 - pins 3 and 15 of P70; - subwoofer in the rear parcel shelf P49 - pins 11, 12 and 25 of P70; the subwoofer P49 is also supplied via the line for fuse F61 of the fuse box in the boot B45. The "ambient" microphone located in the front courtesy light G10 - connector E - is connected to pins 29 and 30 of P70. The aerial P25 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable. A connection lead runs from connector E of P20 to CD player P75:. this cable, is divided into two sections: one under the dashboard and one under the passenger compartment lining (coupling D96).

DESCRIPTION The vehicle is equipped with a radio system comprising: - radio; - front speakers (woofers in the doors and tweeters in the dashboard); - rear speakers located in the doors - cables connecting the radio with the speakers; - aerial with support fitted at the rear of the roof with a coaxial connecting cable. A sophisticated Bose HIFI system with special HIFI speakers and an outside amplifier can also be fitted. The radio is a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and with the other electronic units. The radio is equipped with an anti-theft system through the connection of the radio at the CAN with the Body Computer; it also manages the volume control linked to the vehicle speed: the volume increases and decreases in relation to the speed of the vehicle: this information reaches the radio node via the CAN. Some versions are equipped with a series of buttons on the steering wheel: these make it possible to replicate some of the commands which are acquired in the same way by the actual radio. It is also possible to fit a multi-polar cable connecting the radio to a CD player located in the boot, on the right hand side. See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Radio P20 is supplied directly (4 of connector A) from the battery via the line of fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 . Pin 8 of connector A is earthed. Pins 1 and 3 of connector A receive the CAN line by which the radio P20 is connected to the Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes. The radio P20 is connected, via the CAN, to the radio controls on the steering wheel, via the clock spring D47. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The following cables with signals for the speakers leave connector B of P20: - pins 5 and 6 to the left front speakers P35 and P45; - pins 3 and 4 to the right front speakers P36 and P46; - pins 7 and 8 to the left rear speakers P30 and P47; - pins 1 and 2 to the right rear speakers P31 and P48; The aerial P25 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable. A connection lead runs from connector E of P20 to CD player P75:. this cable, is divided into two sections: one under the dashboard and one under the passenger compartment lining (coupling D96).

DESCRIPTION The handsfree system for Bluetooth phones - built into the dashboard - allows mobile phones to be used on board whilst assuring customer safety and function. - Bluetooth receiver; - integral Voice Recognition unit including microphone (located next to the front courtesy light); - integral Text to Speech unit. - USB interface for Media Player. The control unit is also connected to radio controls on the steering wheel (two special keys for this function are provided in addition to the radio control keys). The alphanumeric display used is that of the control panel. See descriptions 5560 INSTRUMENTS For more details on system operation See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The Bluetooth control unit M162 is supplied directly (pin 16 of connector A) from the battery via the line for fuse F39 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2. The Bluetooth control unit M162 receives an ignition-operated supply (INT) (pin 32 of connector A) via the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2. Pin 15 of connector A of M162 is earthed. The CAN line through which the Bluetooth control unit M162 is connected to the radio P20, the controls on the steering wheel - via the clock spring D47 - the Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes, reaches pins 14 and 30 of connector A. The Bluetooth control unit M162 is connected directly to radio P20 - connector D - from pins 7, 23 and 25 of connector A, sending audio+. audio - and MUTE signals respectively, thus using the radio speakers for voice messages and hands-free communication. In the version with Media Player USB interface, the Bluetooth control unit M162 is connected to radio P20 - connector C - from pins 5, 22 and 21 of connector A with AUX left, AUX right and AUX earth signals. The Media Player USB socket P143 is connected to the Bluetooth control unit M162, to pins 3, 4, 19, 20 and 31 respectively, with signals: signal D+, reference earth, signal D-, 5V power supply and shielding. The hands-free microphone located in the courtesy light G10 is connected to pins 8 and 24 of connector A of M162.
